projects.name: accelerateddecay
projects.summary: A Horizon port of accelerateddecay.
projects.description:
A port of [Accelerated Decay](https://github.com/nanite/AcceleratedDecay) by ErrorMikey (nanite) for Horizon — leaves fall when their log is cut.

**Implemented so far**

- Ready leaves (`distance == 7` and not `persistent`) are removed **one real second** (20 ticks) after a `#minecraft:logs` block is broken, over the mod's 26-neighbour flood fill, which expands only through already-ready leaves.
- The flood keeps per-tick read and removal budgets, retries, a search radius, a merge cap and an age limit: safety valves the port added for pathological modded trees, which the upstream scan does not have.
- A removed leaf's water goes with it (water for a waterlogged leaf, air for a dry one), the same legacy-block rule upstream applies.

**Deviations and gaps**

- **Removal is a plain block set, not a player break.** The pin has no drop-loot, item-entity or cancelable-break API, so a removed leaf drops nothing, no block-break level event fires and no `BLOCK_DESTROY` fires. Recorded as an API gap (a `machine_destroy_block`-style helper).
- The mod ships no blocks, items or data of its own, so this is a code-only mod with no content archive; it also has no config file upstream, so none is written.
- The flood runs on the server tick with the port's budgets, so a very large tree decays over several ticks rather than in one.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/accelerateddecay/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, the full GNU GPL v3 with ErrorMikey's notice) and are also in this repository. GPL-3.0-only; the complete corresponding source is this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

projects.name: Actually Additions
projects.summary: The Coal Generator and Crusher of Actually Additions, with working recipes, real FE and persistence.
projects.description:
A port of [Actually Additions](https://github.com/Ellpeck/ActuallyAdditions) by
Ellpeck for Horizon. This first slice is two machines, carried from the mod's own
jar together with their blocks, items, models, textures, loot tables, recipes and
advancements:

- **Coal Generator** — burns any furnace fuel (modded fuel included) into a
  60,000 FE buffer at 20 FE/t, returning the crafting remainder.
- **Crusher** — a 60,000 FE buffer, 40 FE/t and 100 ticks per operation, reading
  the mod's own `actuallyadditions:crushing` recipes (47 of the jar's 49; two
  name items from later slices) and rolling the second output at its chance.
- A generator pushes FE into an adjacent crusher; there is no Energy Laser Relay
  in this slice, so adjacency is the stand-in.
- Right-click with fuel or an input to insert it; a wrong item is refused. There
  is no screen yet, so `/actuallyadditions info <x> <y> <z>` prints stored FE,
  burn and crusher progress. That command is a port addition, not upstream.

Both machines keep their FE, burn state and crusher output across save and
relaunch. Not yet ported: the GUI/menus, `lit` state and particles, a comparator
output for FE, FE kept in the item when a machine is broken, the machine
crafting recipes' ingredients, the Double Crusher and the other ~45 machines,
relays/cables, redstone control and the booklet. The one `.hnmod` embeds its
content package, so it installs the blocks and the behaviour together.

MIT — the original copyright and licence notices travel inside the bundle
(`mixins/actuallyadditions/LICENSE` and `data/actuallyadditions/license/`), with the
asset provenance in LICENSE-NOTICE.md.

projects.name: ambientsounds
projects.summary: The environment engine with cave and wind ambient beds that fade in and out.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [AmbientSounds](https://github.com/CreativeMD/AmbientSounds) (LGPL-3.0-only, by **CreativeMD** and **AriaFreeze**) for Horizon. This first slice is **the environment engine** and two ambient beds, `cave` and `wind`.

**Implemented so far**

- **The environment scan** runs on the mod's own cadence from its engine file (`environment-tick-time` 40, `sound-tick-time` 4, `block-scan-distance` 40, `biome-scan-distance` 5) and classifies the player by sky access, depth below the surface, rain/thunder and the surrounding biome.
- **Two ambient beds** play through Horizon's music layers with a real fade: in a sealed cave the `cave` bed rises to full gain over 20 ticks, on an open platform it aims to zero and fades out, and **during a thunderstorm the `wind` bed takes over**.
- **Vanilla music is held** while a bed plays and is released when it fades; an "engine off" setting makes the mod silent.
- **Two of the mod's 120 sound files are carried** (about 2 MB of 85 MB), and the build checks that every carried byte is the jar's own.

**Not yet ported**

- the other 118 sound files and their beds (animals, water, weather, suspense);
- the air-pocket block scan and its block groups (so the cave bed currently follows depth and sky, not every cave shape);
- the cross-fade between takes, the pitch curves, the config GUI and the other regions.

**Licence.** LGPL-3.0-only. The port ships the LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts and a notice naming **CreativeMD** and **AriaFreeze**, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256; it is a derivative under the same licence and its complete source is published, with no further restriction added.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

projects.name: AppleSkin (Horizon)
projects.summary: Shows the saturation hidden behind your hunger bar, and what a food item will restore.
projects.description:
Vanilla keeps your saturation invisible: you see twenty hunger points and nothing about the buffer sitting behind them. AppleSkin draws it, so you can tell when a golden carrot is worth eating and when it is wasted.

- Saturation in gold along the top of the hunger bar, half an icon per point, filling right to left as the hunger icons do.
- Food values in tooltips: `Hunger +N` and `Saturation +N.N`, read from the item's own `minecraft:food` component, so food from content mods shows its numbers too.
- Settings under Options > Mods > AppleSkin: the mod on or off, the saturation overlay, the tooltip lines.

It only reads the numbers the game already has and draws on the HUD. Nothing leaves your computer, and it works on any server because it is entirely client-side.

An independent MIT implementation that follows [AppleSkin](https://github.com/squeek502/AppleSkin) by squeek502 (The Unlicense) without copying its code or artwork; see the NOTICE in the source.

projects.name: artifacts
projects.summary: A Horizon port of artifacts.
projects.description:
A port of [Artifacts](https://github.com/ochotonida/artifacts) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- Three artifacts, each with the upstream effect rules in a pure runtime: `artifacts:bunny_hoppers` (jump strength +0.40 multiplied-base, safe fall distance +10, fall damage multiplier unchanged), `artifacts:feral_claws` (attack speed +0.30 multiplied-base) and `artifacts:shock_pendant` (cancels a hit whose damage type is in the lightning tag).
- Upstream equips artifacts in its own equipment slots (Curios on 1.21.1). This slice **defers the slot system**: the main inventory and off hand stand in for the worn slots, and each artifact counts at most once, like one slot.
- The attributes are re-applied every player tick, so dropping or disabling an artifact removes its modifiers.
- A right click moves a main-hand artifact into an **empty off hand** (refused when the off hand is occupied).
- The items' models, textures, language entries and creative tab.

**Not yet ported**

- **Inventory instead of slots.** A player can carry all three at once, and a second copy of one artifact adds nothing (one slot per kind).
- **Upstream's own equipment slots** (and Curios) are not carried; the off-hand equip is the stand-in.
- The other artifacts of the mod, their configs and the durability/repair behaviour are later slices.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) Wouter Pauwels`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 3: the off hand is now the only worn slot. Until this version any artifact anywhere in the inventory counted, so carrying one was the same as wearing it — the Feral Claws gave +30% attack speed from a backpack slot. Now only the off hand grants an effect, and a carried duplicate adds nothing. Equip path unchanged; the off hand is not replaced when occupied, and an unknown id is refused.
First release

projects.name: Horizon Auto Fishing
projects.summary: Reels in when a fish bites and casts again, with break protection, inventory rod swapping and random delays.
projects.description:
Horizon Auto Fishing automates fishing input: it sends raw use_item packets to reel in on the bite and cast again, and uses inventory clicks to swap rods and throw away junk. You cast first by hand — the mod never casts on its own — and it takes over from there.

Many servers forbid AFK or automated fishing, or may flag it with an anticheat, so using this mod can get you banned. Check the server's rules first.

Break protection keeps a rod from being used once 5 or fewer durability remain, and the all-rods modes swap a worn-out rod for the freshest rod in your hotbar or inventory. Delays get a small random extra (up to 5 ticks by default). The opt-in junk filter throws away only the items you list — while it is on, it drops one listed item per tick, even when you are not fishing.

versions.changelog: Ships the MIT LICENSE file inside the .hmod, fixes the version mismatch, and rewrites the description to disclose automated fishing input and the ban risk. Bite detection unchanged from 1.0.2.

projects.name: Auto Login
projects.summary: Detects login/register prompts in chat and logs you in or registers you, per server.
projects.description:
Auto Login watches for login and register prompts — in chat, in the action bar and on the boss bar — and acts on them: when the server asks you to log in, it sends /login with the password saved for that server and player; when the server asks you to register and no password is saved, it generates a random password, sends /register, and saves it for next time.

Manual commands /autologin and /autoregister do the same on demand, and /autologin set, pattern, delay, toggle and status configure it without rebuilding.

Passwords are stored in plain text on the device, one line per server, in the mod's own data files — use a password made just for that server.

versions.changelog: Boss-bar prompts are now deduplicated per bar and per connection, so two bars on screen no longer re-trigger processing each frame; the mod manifest now declares the MIT license.
The .hmod now also reads action-bar (overlay) chat lines for login/register prompts. Title text has no hook in the mod API, so title-only prompts are caught by the .hnmod only.

projects.name: Bells & Whistles
projects.summary: Bells & Whistles' decorative station, metro and train blocks for Horizon: 36 blocks — the andesite/brass/copper grab rails, bogie steps and door steps,…
projects.description:
Bells & Whistles' decorative station, metro and train blocks for Horizon: 36 blocks — the andesite/brass/copper grab rails, bogie steps and door steps, the headlight, the ornate iron trapdoor, the station platform, the metro casing/panel/trapdoor/window set and eighteen pilots — with their block items, self-drop loot tables, 44 carried recipes, the climbable and mineable/pickaxe tags and one creative tab. The blocks copy vanilla templates (ladder, lever, iron trapdoor, carved pumpkin, end rod, iron block), because the original's Create classes do not exist here; the headlight therefore keeps a lever's powered state and toggles on right click, and the nine Create-only polished-cut pilots have no recipe. There is no block entity, entity, menu, renderer, config or network code: the original mod at 0.4.7 ships none.

**Implemented so far:** the slice in the package, as described above.

**Not yet ported**

- **Create is not ported.** The wrench behaviour, Create's panel placement helper and copycat face-hiding, and the train-door forms (`folding_metro_door`, `sliding_metro_door`) are deferred — the two door forms are not registered by `ModBlocks` at 0.4.7 anyway.
- **The headlight uses `minecraft:lever`.** Its `powered` state and right-click toggle are a template artefact; the light is constant 15.
- **Custom shapes** for the rails, headlight and pilots are not declared.
- **Nine pilots have no recipe** (Create's polished-cut stones).
- **Recipe materials are substituted**; the recipes are not upstream's exact ingredients, because Create is absent.
- **Stonecutting recipes are carried but not crafted in the e2e.** The crafting path is proved for six recipes; the stonecutter menu path is not exercised.
- **The creative tab's position** differs from upstream, which inserts into vanilla tabs; Horizon content mods cannot.
- **Map colour** is the template's (upstream copied mossy cobblestone/stone colours) and was not visually checked headless.

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0`, not "or later" — the pinned jar's own `neoforge.mods.toml` declares `license="GPL-3.0"`, its `LICENSE` is the GPL version 3 text, and the "or any later version" wording appears only in that text's generic application example, not in a project-specific grant.

Ported to Horizon 0.2 from the upstream mod; pinned to game 26.3, Horizon SDK `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. The full corresponding source ships in this repository beside the artifact.

Based on the original project: https://github.com/aesefficio/BellsAndWhistlesMod

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the carried-recipe family: 44 files were carried and only 6 had ever been crafted, with all 10 stonecutting files unexercised. Every one now crafts in a real game — 30 through a crafting table and 10 through the stonecutter menu — asserting the output id and count and that the inputs were consumed. Four real defects surfaced on the way. Upstream names `c:ingots/brass` and `c:ingots/copper`, and the carry mapped both to copper, so four brass grids were byte-identical to their copper counterparts and one could never win; brass now maps to gold, one-to-one with copper. Four `*_pilot_from_cut` files were byte-duplicates of their base file and are dropped. Andesite's door step filled vanilla's `andesite_slab` grid, which is the vanilla-shadow class, and now uses a two-wide pattern; the validator gained a rule that fails any such grid. And the headlight pair is kept as one grid with a test pinning it. The harness fact is recorded too: a station must be opened with `interact` beside it, not `use`, or every slot click silently misses.
First publication in the SDK format.

A Horizon port of [YUNG's Better Desert Temples](https://github.com/YUNG-GANG/YUNGs-Better-Desert-Temples) (LGPL-3.0, by **YUNGNICKYOUNG** and **Acarii**) for Horizon. projects.name: YUNG's Better Dungeons
projects.summary: YUNG's Better Dungeons for Horizon, slice 1: the small dungeon. The port registers its own structure type (betterdungeons:small_dungeon_type), which…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [YUNG's Better Dungeons 1.21.1-NeoForge-5.1.4](https://github.com/YUNG-GANG/YUNGs-Better-Dungeons) by **YUNGNICKYOUNG and Acarii** (**LGPL-3.0-only**), slice 1: the small dungeon.

**Implemented so far**

- The mod's structures are assembled by `yungsapi:yung_jigsaw`, a Java structure type 26.3 does not have, so the port registers its own type, `betterdungeons:small_dungeon_type`, which does the assembly the Java type did: it draws a start element from the jar's carried template pool by the jar's rules, rotates and places the pieces and hands the result to the engine.
- It carries sixteen `.nbt` shells and loot piles, two template pools with their weights and `max_counts`, and four processor chains, and it decorates the result with the eleven `betterdungeons:*` processors the data calls — the dungeon banners, the mob spawner, the chest and banner caps, the ceiling props, the support legs, and the rule processor that turns air into cave air.
- A saved bounding box's span is checked in 64-bit and clamped per axis before any allocation, so a malformed save cannot make the support leg scan to the void.
- The port was proven in game at 0.2.1: the launcher-built package passes, and a game without it fails at the first step.

**Not yet ported**

- **Only one of the five structures.** `skeleton_dungeon`, `zombie_dungeon`, `small_nether_dungeon` and `spider_dungeon` are not carried; the last two use the mod's own Java structure types with hand-written pieces, so they are a later slice with their own structure types.
- **The two `remove_*_feature_in` biome modifiers** are not carried: they remove vanilla dungeons by tag, which is a separate feature the engine's biome-modifier registrar would express.
- **The config file** is not carried — the defaults are compiled in, so there is no config screen and no `enableHeads` / `enableNetherBlocks` / `enableOreProps` toggle at run time.
- **`start_height`'s `x_offset_in_chunk` / `z_offset_in_chunk`** are not implemented beyond the default 0 the jar omits; a pack that sets either is refused.
- **Saved pieces are re-derived from the template**, not from a stored block list, so a structure saved by a different mod version loads its template through this port's processor chain.
- **Liquid settings**: the jar's `liquid_settings: ignore_waterlogging` is carried and reported, but the port writes the template's own states rather than implementing waterlogging behaviour, so the engine's liquid handling is what applies.
- **`spawn_overrides`** are carried empty and not read, because the engine ignores them for a mod's structures.

Upstream's licence and notice travel inside the package. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

projects.name: YUNG's Better Mineshafts
projects.summary: YUNG's Better Mineshafts 5.1.1 for Horizon: the mod's own mineshaft geometry, generated in Rust behind an SDK structure type. The jar has no templates at…
projects.description:
YUNG's Better Mineshafts 5.1.1 for Horizon: the mod's own mineshaft geometry, generated in
Rust behind an SDK structure type. The jar has no templates at all (0 .nbt, 0 pools, 0 processor
lists) — its mineshaft is a Java structure type that builds ten piece classes in code — so this
port carries the jar's thirteen structure definitions with their per-variant palettes and writes
the geometry itself: a vertical entrance shaft with ladder and doorway, a 9x8x24 main corridor with
planks, fence supports, rails, lanterns, cobwebs and gravel piles, a 5x5x8 branch corridor and a
10x5x5 workstation room, from the seed and the structure's own config. The other pieces (stairs,
turns, layered intersections, ore deposits, zombie-villager rooms, surface tunnels, minecarts and
biome decorations) are recorded gaps in notes.md.

**Implemented so far:** the slice in the package, as described above.

**Not yet ported**

- **The in-game leg passes — what it does *not* yet cover.** The three legs are green (below), but
- **Biome decorations:** addBiomeDecorations (BetterMineshaftPiece.java:175-240) places
- **Corridor legs (edge/inner):** BigTunnel.generateLegsVariant1/2 (BigTunnel.java:253-369)
- **Surface tunnel:** VerticalEntrance.determineDirection (VerticalEntrance.java:300-361)

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the bookcase and the shelf become storage. The bookcase takes 16 slots of books only and answers a comparator with the highest slot holding a redstone book; the shelf takes 4 slots of anything; both are reachable by hoppers on every face, spill their contents when broken, and the redstone book item ships with its shapeless recipe. Proven in game with the values read from the world rather than the code: the bookcase menu shows 16 slots, a plain book in slot 5 leaves the wire at 0 while a redstone book in slot 3 raises it to 3 and moving it to slot 1 drops it back to 0, the bookcase refuses stone where the shelf accepts it, a hopper moves three books and the break drops two, and a vanilla barrel beside it shows 27 slots and takes the stone the bookcase refused. The enchanting bonus is left as a measured gap rather than faked: the pin declares the hook but the game never calls it and counts a static tag of provider blocks instead, so putting the bookcase in that tag would make an empty bookcase worth a whole bookshelf — the leg asserts the gap so it fails when the pin fixes it. Two findings are recorded for other ports: opening a mod container needs the mod's own `right_click_block` calling `open_menu`, because a plain click opens nothing even with the menu declared, and a block whose contents the engine already spills must not also carry `block_entity_data` or it double-carries.

projects.name: Big Nukes
projects.summary: Nuclear bombs whose shockwave digs real craters and leaves fallout. Launch missiles, build a superbomb, survive in a bunker.
projects.description:
**One mod, one file, on Horizon's new mod API.** 0.4.0 carries its textures, models, sounds, text and recipes inside it. Your bombs, zones and bunkers stay.

- **Make** the bombs: mine uranium below y=16, enrich it in a centrifuge, and put the parts together on the assembly table.
- **Blast** with a demolition charge (radius 16), a tactical warhead (50), an atomic bomb (250), a neutron bomb that kills but leaves the buildings standing, or a dirty bomb. The flash, the mushroom cloud and the ring of the shockwave are seen from far beyond your render distance, and the wave leaves a crater, ash and fires behind it.
- **Set them off** by fuse, by a keypad's code, or by a remote from any distance. Fire a missile, or a splitting missile with three warheads, from a silo at coordinates up to 4096 blocks away, or call a bomber onto a strike beacon. A siren wails at a launch.
- **Build** the Sunbreaker round its core: 26 implosion shells and 98 neutron reflectors, radius 600 to 1000. At 1000 it breaks through the bedrock.
- **Survive** the radiation: a Geiger counter, a hazmat suit, anti-rad, iodine tablets, and a decontaminator that turns the ash back to grass.
- **Weather** what follows the first blast: radioactive storms, mutants in the zones and falling satellites, which a powered radar warns of.
- **Hide** in a bunker: reinforced and armored concrete, a multilayer wall that holds even the Sunbreaker away from its center, a hermetic door, and an air filter powered by a fuel generator that keeps 95% of the radiation out of a sealed room.

The Big Nukes Guide tells it all in the game. English and Russian.

**Commands:** `/bignukes guide` gives the guide. Operators have `/bignukes blast <radius> [x y z]`, `/bignukes maxpower [16|50|250|1000|1024]`, the largest blast a world allows, and `/bignukes events`, which turns the storms, mutants and satellites on or off.

Native source mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, press Build there, and confirm the native-code warning. The launcher compiles it against the Horizon build it is pinned to, named in each version's changelog. It runs with your account's permissions.

All the art and sounds are original. No Minecraft code or assets are included. MIT licensed.

Reactivated as one native .hmod on Horizon's mod API: the code and all the content in one package. Same blocks and world files, so your bombs, zones and bunkers stay. New since 0.2.0: the neutron bomb, the dirty bomb, the splitting missile, the siren and launch notices; radioactive storms, mutants and falling satellites after a world's first blast, with a radar that warns of them. - **Fluids** — the 10 fluid blocks, coolants, steam, the fluid ports and the reactor's active cooling mode.

- **The reinforced variant** (1.0 efficiency, 1,000-block maximum, 30,000 FE part capacity), **control-rod insertion**, **solid moderators** and **waste ejection**.
- **GUIs** — the controller's screen, the port's in/out mode, the redstone port and the computer ports; and the Patchouli guide book.

versions.changelog: The four findings of the review on this pull request, each reproduced against the delivered 0.2.4 before it was fixed. One formation record per machine: the shape is built once and shared through an Arc behind every block that answers for the machine, controllers and ports alike, so four controllers no longer hold four copies of a five-thousand-block shell, which was three hundred and eighty-one mebibytes of duplicated coordinates. Ports are visited once per machine per tick, claimed by a single master controller, and a switched-off machine visits none at all — asserted as a count of visits, not a wall time, so it cannot be satisfied by a faster machine. A port's capability access now re-derives its membership from the world instead of trusting a saved coordinate and a formed bit, so a port left outside after a machine is rebuilt smaller answers nothing; the in-game run shows the detached old port reading not formed while the new one works. And the reactor takes only the fuel its tank has room for, writing the remainder back into the slot, which the access port now shows as three ingots where the old package left it empty.

Slice 2 (the energizer), the bounded-tick-cost repair, and the budget fix. Adds the energizer, the fourth multiblock — its 3x3x3 to 32-cubed forms, the cell count and capacity, the controller and the four blocks, on/off with FE in and out — with four defects fixed (carried recipes named c: common tags Horizon never resolves; the blocks were missing from minecraft:mineable/pickaxe; the power tap pushed its buffer back into the reactor; two graphite_from_coalblock recipes were dead data). Structure work is bounded: scans are shared per component, invalidation is limited to the affected topology (inside the box always, the one-block ring only when a machine part sits there, another level never), and SCANS_PER_TICK = 4 is paid from a budget refilled at level_tick_post. This version closes the remaining bypass: a capability scan — an energizer tick asking an adjacent machine's capacity — was charged Budget::Once, so every such tick did an unbudgeted scan. The budget now opens at level_tick_pre and closes at level_tick_post, so in-tick capability scans come out of the same share, while clicks, commands and one-off capability calls still cost one scan and a cache hit is free in both. Proven in game: an energizer fills two adjacent reactors (9,253 -> 216,000 FE); one tick that invalidates five machines runs 4 fresh scans and the rest report not-formed; with the old policy the same scenario runs 7 (counterfactual EXIT:1); all five recover once the casings are replaced.
First release

projects.name: Bridging Mod
projects.summary: A port of Bridging Mod for Horizon: a right click in the air with a placeable block item fills the gap the player looks into, so a bridge can be built…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Bridging Mod 2.7.0: right-click in the air with a placeable block item while looking into a gap over an edge, and the block lands in the gap instead of requiring a block to aim at. Upstream does this on the client, while this port computes the same target from the acting player's eye ray on the server, so it works in single player and on a server with no client mod. Upstream: https://github.com/squeeglii/BridgingMod — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- A right click **in the air** walks the eye ray from 20 % of the reach to the reach, in vanilla's main-hand-then-off-hand order.
- The first cell along that ray is taken when it is replaceable, outside the player's box, and next to a solid non-liquid block on a side the view points into.
- The held block is placed there, one item is consumed (none in creative), the place sound and the `used` statistic fire, and a stack's `minecraft:block_entity_data` is applied only for a player who may use game-master blocks.
- Every placement check runs before anything is written: build permission, item use at the position, the world border, a dedicated server's spawn protection, and an unobstructed destination.
- Torches are skipped as upstream does, a cell inside the player's own body is skipped while the search continues, and anything the assist cannot place falls through to vanilla.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.2 with a control game that does not fill the gap and a selftest that inverts the assertion.

**Not yet ported**

- The placed state is the block's default state plus the item's `minecraft:block_state` component rather than vanilla's `getStateForPlacement` from a fake hit, because the pin has no query for one, so a bridged stair or log keeps its default facing and loses that much fidelity.
- The state's own survival rule is not consulted, because no `canSurvive`-shaped query exists at this pin.
- `minecraft:placed_block` never fires, because the SDK refuses `minecraft:` criteria, so advancement triggers do not see a bridged placement.
- `EntityPlaceEvent` is not fired, so a mod that cancels placements does not see a bridged one.
- On a LAN guest the crosshair check uses the server's eye ray rather than the guest's reported hit, since no forced-hit read is exposed.
- The client effects, the keybind and config screen, and the slab and perspective alignment helpers are not ported, because they are client-only by design.
- The special-item compatibility layer for DankStorage, BankStorage, PlaceableItem and Sable is not carried, and a refused placement is silent, since a native mod may not add a logging crate.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: buildinggadgets2
projects.summary: A Horizon port of buildinggadgets2.
projects.description:
A port of [Building Gadgets 2](https://github.com/Direwolf20-MC/BuildingGadgets2) (MIT, by Direwolf20 and the Building Gadgets contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **building gadget** and its horizontal-row mode.

**Implemented so far**

- `buildinggadgets2:gadget_building` (stack size 1) right-clicked on a block. **Sneak + right click** selects the clicked block's state (upstream's `onShiftAction`); air, unbreakable blocks and non-source fluids are refused. **Plain right click** builds the selected block's **horizontal row**: `side = face.axis == Y ? player facing : -face`, cells `clicked + side*i` for `i in 0..range`, skipping cells that are not replaceable, outside the build height, or where the state cannot survive.
- Each placed cell consumes one item of the block's kind; creative pays nothing. A gadget with no selection, no items or no room places nothing and says why.
- The selection/range state is stored **as an item component** (`buildinggadgets2:gadget_state`), so it travels with the gadget and survives a relog, and the mouse wheel changes the range through the `mouse_scrolling` client hook (`scroll.rs`).
- `/buildinggadgets2` readout commands for the harness, with the carried model, texture, language and recipe inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

projects.summary: A Horizon port of bwncr.
projects.description:
A port of [Bad Wither No Cookie Reloaded](https://gitlab.com/kreezxil/BadWitherNoCookie) (MIT, by Kreezxil and Eleksploded) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The decision data and the harness surface for upstream's sound silencing: the wither spawn (`entity.wither.spawn`, exact) and wither death (`entity.wither.death`, case-insensitive) sound names, plus the wandering trader's ambient and the llama's ambient, with `/bwncr listen|heard|silence` recording and printing the decisions the hook will use.
- The three carried language files (`en_us`, `es_ar`, `pt_br`) from the jar, inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported, and this is the important part**

- **The suppression itself is not carried.** The pin has no client-side "a sound is about to play" hook: `native-hooks.json` contains no sound or audio entry, and `play_sound_to` is still pending and unstamped. The named hook request is NeoForge's `PlaySoundEvent` — sound id, category, position, volume, pitch, **cancellable**. Until that hook is stamped this port silences nothing; `/bwncr` reports the decisions such a hook would make.
- `/bwncr listen` prints through `/bwncr heard` rather than live: upstream sends each name to the player's chat as it arrives client-side, and this slice collects them instead.

So: installing this mod currently changes no sound. It exists to hold the decision table and the command surface for the slice that lands when the hook does. MIT — the licence is declared by the jar the pack ships (`META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, `license="MIT"`; upstream publishes no LICENSE file), and the notice travels inside the archive at `mixins/bwncr/LICENSE`.

projects.name: centered_crosshair
projects.summary: A Horizon port of Centered Crosshair.
projects.description:
centered-crosshair, ported 1:1 to Horizon from JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair (MIT (c) 2023 JustAlittleWolf, https://github.com/JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair).  Upstream is entirely render-side and tiny (4 Java files, 176 LOC). Vanilla draws the crosshair with integer blit coordinates, `x = (w - 15) / 2` in gui-scaled pixels, where `w` is an integer that already lost its fraction to `floor(windowWidth / guiScale)`. When the gui-scaled size is even the sprite lands half a pixel off the true window centre. This port keeps the sprite centred at the real centre, computed from the raw window size, quantised to quarter pixels, and drawn through a subpixel textured-quad path with the sprite's u/v nudged by a 1/32768 half-texel so linear sampling reads the sprite edges cleanly.  Upstream structure mapped 1:1:

Port by sparticle. Upstream: https://github.com/JustAlittleWolf/centered-crosshair (MIT).

Source-only .hmod built on the current SDK (Horizon f00125f)

Licence: MIT. Source: https://github.com/Sparticle62ops/horizon-centered-crosshair

projects.description:

**Implemented so far**

- **The chisel converts on a mining attempt**, as upstream's `ChiselItem.canMine` does: with a chisel in hand, left-clicking a block that belongs to a chisel group replaces it with the next member of that group and cancels the break, so the chisel never mines. One press converts exactly one block (implemented on the dig's start event, which is cancellable).
- **The andesite family, carried whole:** 32 variants — 30 plain cubes, the two `axis` variants (`pillar`, `twist`) and the three weighted-model variants (`chaotic_bricks`, `cut`, `french`) — with their blockstates, 58 block models, 32 item models and item definitions, 61 textures, 32 loot tables, the language file, the chisel item and its recipe, and the pickaxe tag.

- **Block shapes follow upstream's registration:** `PillarBlock` (an `axis` property, default `y`) for the `pillar`/`twist` styles, a plain `Block` for the rest, both copying andesite's settings; the item is a single-stack tool with a mining-speed bonus and one shaped recipe (iron ingot + stick).

**Not yet ported**

- the other block materials and their families (only `andesite` is carried in this slice);
- the chisel GUI, the "chiseled" templates and the remaining styles of other materials;
- the mod's own advancement/tab beyond the carried creative tab entry.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository (GPL-2.0 text and a NOTICE naming the authors). Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

projects.description:
A port of [Compact Machines](https://github.com/CompactMods/CompactMachines) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- `/compactmachines info`, `list`, `enter`, `leave` and `rooms` (upstream has no commands; these are the port's harness surface, like `/powah info`).

| Template | Interior | Shell |
|---|---|---|
| tiny | 3 × 3 × 3 | 5³ (98 blocks) |
| small | 5 × 5 × 5 | 7³ |
| normal | 7 × 7 × 7 | 9³ (386 blocks) |
| large | 9 × 9 × 9 | 11³ |
| giant | 11 × 11 × 11 | 13³ |
| colossal | 13 × 13 × 13 | 15³ |

**Not yet ported**

- The compact dimension itself, its biome and dimension files: rooms live in a **reserved volume of the Overworld** instead (see below), which is a visible, persistent world change.
- The room generator's structures and floors beyond the sealed shell; the preview screen; room upgrades; the PSD's keybinds; Jade/JEI/Curios; the villager; the gamerules; out-of-bounds damage and the teleport veto.
- A room's shell is the unbreakable `solid_wall`, not upstream's breakable `wall` (the pin has no teleport veto, so a breakable shell would leak into the Overworld); `wall` is carried and craftable.
- The PSD cooldown is server-side (25 ticks); the pin has no item-cooldown helper.
- **The rooms are a permanent modification of the Overworld.** Each room occupies a 64-block region starting at (30000, 200, 30000) and is built on first entry. A site is only used when its whole volume (shell **and** interior) is empty air: an occupied site is skipped and the room moves to the next free one, so no player build is overwritten and nobody is enclosed in a solid interior. A room that has been built stays built (`built` is saved) and its shell cannot be broken by a player.

projects.description:
A port of [CC: Tweaked](https://github.com/cc-tweaked/CC-Tweaked) 1.121.0 for Horizon — the **Computer** block, with a terminal that runs a program.

**Implemented in this slice**

- `computercraft:computer_normal` — `facing` × `state` (`off`/`on`/`blinking`) on the stone template, upstream's blockstate model chain (`minecraft:block/orientable` with the computer's own front/side/top textures and the lit screen while running), a block entity declared in code, self-drop loot, the upstream crafting shape with 26.3 ingredients, and a creative tab.

**Not yet ported**

- **The ROM**: 105 Lua files (`bios.lua`, 20 `rom/apis`, 23 `rom/modules`, 60 `rom/programs`) and the shell. That needs a real Lua 5.2 VM, and the pin's lock blocks the engine route (see the port's record), so the engine is the unblocker.
- **Language features**: tables, functions and closures, `break`, `repeat`, `in`/generic `for`, multiple returns and assignment, metamethods, `pcall`/`error`, the string/table/math/os libraries, `require`/`dofile`, coroutines (the basis of every CC API), varargs, `#` on tables, integer division `//`, `goto`, long strings, hex literals and `\ddd` escapes.
- Peripherals, modems/rednet, monitors, disk drives, printers, speakers, turtles, pocket computers, the GUI and the remaining 15 blockstates.

The four upstream CCPL textures are **regenerated** by `tools/gen_textures.py` (documented palette, byte-identical `--check`) because CCPL §7 forbids reusing them in another game — no upstream pixel is carried. Original copyright and licence notices travel in the package. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the peripheral surface: a computer can now ask a block beside it what it is and call a method on it. A capability key of this package's own, a peripheral trait with a type name, a method list and one call at a time, the six-side geometry relative to the computer's facing, and the three interpreter builtins getType, getNames and call, with a harness block shipped as the probe. Proven in game with three neighbours at once: a harness on the right answers its type and its methods and round-trips a string and adds two numbers, while a plain stone on the left and air above answer nil for every call, and an unknown method is a named error rather than silence. The stone neighbour is asserted present before the call, so nil cannot be an empty side. A second carriage-return-shaped trap is recorded with it: the one-block terminal is sixteen columns, so the type wraps mid-name and the assertion compares the exact bytes rather than a substring. This is the surface a whole family of add-ons was waiting on; three deviations are stated rather than hidden, including that getNames answers one tab-separated line because the interpreter has no tables yet.

projects.description:
A port of [Create: Hypertube](https://github.com/PedroRok/CreateHypertubes) by Rok for Horizon. Ride a tube run from an entrance to its far mouth at the jar's own travel speed.

**Implemented so far**

- **Hypertube and Hyper Entrance** — placed with their facing and axis from the look, tube neighbours update `connected`/`east_west`/`north_south`/`up_down` on place and break.
- **The travel rule with the jar's numbers** — a run needs the cell behind the mouth and the 3-point minimum, moves at **0.5 blocks/tick** at the minimum powered speed, exits **1.5 blocks past the far entrance**, and a 40-tick re-entry guard stops instant re-entry.
- **Controls that hold** — an entrance facing air moves nobody, a lone tube moves nobody, and a wall ends the ride at the far entrance without damage.

**Not yet ported**

- **Kinetic power and accelerators.** Create's rotation cannot be linked from a separate mod, so the speed is the jar's minimum; `travel_speed(rpm)` is already implemented and tested at 8/16/32/256 rpm for the slice that adds it.
- Curves, junctions, splitters, the funnel and smart-tube attachments.
- The client half: detached camera, swim pose, particles and sound, the bezier renderer and the escape keybind.
- Non-player travellers and the entity-list config; tube collision (content collision cannot depend on the entity, so tubes are walk-through).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository (Apache-2.0, Rok). Pinned to Horizon `1d63e0a` and horizon-mixins `5a64af93` for game 26.3.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, every living traveller rides: villagers and other living entities now travel the tube beside players, where only server players did. The rules are the jar's own — a default blacklist holding the wither and the ender dragon, living entities only, a spectator never riding, sneak refusing the pull, and a ride table keyed by entity UUID — with the entity sweep every ten ticks and a traveller standing in the cell its feet are in. Proven in game: the player reaches x 223.0 at half a block a tick while a villager follows from 199.5 to 223.0 on the same path, a dropped item and a wither stay put over forty ticks, sneaking holds the traveller at 199.5 until the key is released, and both the tube and the entrance recipes craft with their ingredients consumed while nine copper crafts nothing. The accelerators, junctions and funnel stay recorded gaps for a stated reason: they read Create's kinetic network, which cannot be linked at this pin, so carrying one would mean inventing a no-power speed; curves need the bezier renderer and a corner model a content block cannot express.

projects.summary: A Horizon port of createaddition.
projects.description:
A port of [Create Crafts & Additions](https://github.com/mrh0/createaddition) for Horizon — the electric (FE) half of the mod, with the jar's own transfer rates. Upstream is **MIT**, by **MRH0**.

**Implemented**

- `createaddition:connector` (small) and `createaddition:large_connector` — 1,000 FE/t and 5,000 FE/t each way, declared through `block_entity_energy` as `Capabilities.Energy.BLOCK`. Placed against a face, `facing` points at the block it is mounted on.
- `createaddition:modular_accumulator` — 2,000,000 FE storage, 5,000 FE/t each way.
- Seven items: `copper_wire`, `gold_wire`, `electrum_wire`, `spool`, `copper_spool`, `gold_spool`, `electrum_spool`.
- Placement mode, as upstream's `ConnectorMode.test` decides on the first server tick: a mounted block that can give is **pulled** from, one that can only take is **pushed** into, else none. `/createaddition mode` sets it (upstream uses Create's wrench, which is not installed here).

**Not yet ported**

- The rotation half: `electric_motor`, `alternator`, `rolling_mill`, `tesla_coil`, `servo_motor`, and the `charging/` recipe type (40+ oxidisation and charging recipes). Create is a separate native mod with no mod-to-mod API, so these blocks cannot join its kinetic network — a recorded gap, not an omission.
- `small_light_connector` (its 1 FE/t lamp consumption) and `creative_energy`.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository, and the upstream author is credited above. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 5, the small light connector: the lamp variant of the small connector, which draws one FE a tick from its network and lights after a period that depends on where it stands, then darkens just as slowly when the energy stops. The period is the reference's own hash of the block's position, ten to twenty-eight ticks, and the counter clamps, so a lamp that has gone dark needs twice its period of energy before it lights again — the game leg waits that long and says why, rather than pretending the first figure was wrong. Proven in game with the numbers: at no energy the lamp is unpowered and its emitted light reads zero; seeded with five thousand and linked it is powered, its light reads fifteen, and the source falls forty-two FE over forty-two ticks, exactly one a tick, with the source, the pool and the lamp's draw adding up. Unlinked, it darkens and the source stops falling. This is also the first slice whose second build check is red, and that is the honest result: the light emission handle this family needs does not exist in the older build, so the pin run is not a tautology. Recorded in the notes for whoever repins next.

Slice 4, the redstone relay: a wire block that passes energy only while it has a redstone signal, with two separate ports so the input pool and the output pool are different networks rather than one, and a thousand FE of in-flight energy that is conserved across the gap. The gate is what the slice is about: unpowered, nothing crosses and the sink stays exactly where it was; powered, twenty-four thousand and twenty FE arrive and the books balance to the last FE, with the block's own `powered` state read back before and after the redstone block is placed. The reference has no energy capability on this block, so none was declared here either — declaring one would let a neighbour bypass the gate entirely, and that is recorded as a deviation from our brief rather than from the mod. A selftest that trips the conservation assertion fails, and a second one that flips the gate fails on its own, so the two claims are independent. One harness defect is recorded with the fix: a local variable shadowed the readout's field name through bash's dynamic scoping, which made a restore branch never run and produced a false no-movement reading.

The tower plan is linear in the number of disconnected accumulators, proven by counting set lookups rather than wall time; a saved tower outside the three by five limit is refused before any capacity arithmetic and a controller near the coordinate limit no longer overflows; and the upstream MIT notice travels inside the package verbatim. Credit: a port of Create Crafts & Additions by MRH0, https://github.com/MRH0/createaddition.
First release

projects.name: Data Exporter
projects.summary: Saves what happens in your game and your statistics to files on your computer, ready to analyze.
projects.description:
Turns what happens in your game into data you own. While you play, Data Exporter saves events and statistics to files on your computer, ready to analyze with DuckDB, pandas, Spark or a spreadsheet.

Nothing is sent over the network. It only writes to the folder you choose.

**What it saves**

- Session & player: joining and leaving, dimension changes, and a sample of position, health and food every 5 seconds.
- Blocks & combat: blocks broken and placed with their coordinates, your deaths, and the mobs you kill.
- Items & progress: crafting, items picked up, and advancements.
- Statistics: every increase of the game's statistics, at the moment it happens.

By default it only saves your own data. Other players' data, typed text and keyboard input are not captured.

**How to use it**

Options > Mods > Data Exporter > Config has one switch per group and the format (JSON Lines or CSV). In a world, `/data_exporter` says what was saved and where your profile is, and `/data_exporter open` shows it in your file manager.

Files go to `data-exporter/` in your game folder, one file per kind of data, world and session.

**Your profile**

Everything is in `config/data_exporter.json`. Edit it while playing and the mod picks it up within a second. There you can turn each kind of data on or off, send one to its own folder or format, and set size limits. When the folder reaches its limit, the mod stops saving until you free space or raise the limit. It never deletes your data.

Source and full documentation: https://github.com/DylanGonzaloFerreyra/horizon-data-exporter

projects.name: Daybreak
projects.summary: Sun shadows, reflective water, waving plants, coloured light, sun rays and bloom, built to cost as little GPU time as possible.
projects.description:
Daybreak is a shader pack in Horizon's own format. It runs inside Horizon's renderer, so Horizon's culling, batching and LOD stay in charge, and it adds as little GPU time as it can.

- Sun and moon shadows with smooth edges
- Warm sunlight, blue sky light in the shade, a dim blue night
- Coloured block light: soul fire blue, redstone red, copper green, froglights
- Light from torches in your hand (turn on Horizon's Dynamic lights in Extras)
- Waving leaves, grass, flowers and crops
- Water with waves, reflections, refraction and the sun's glint
- A deeper sky with warm sunsets, sun rays, sun glare and haze
- Mobs take the sun's shadow; the Nether and the End get their own light
- Linear light and HDR on Horizon's final shader API 0.2

Every effect can be changed or turned off in the game: Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. The quality is yours to pick there too: turn shadows off for the least GPU time, or choose the shadow map's detail (1024 to 4096) and distance (48 to 160 blocks). The defaults are soft shadows over 64 blocks with screen-space water reflections; the full water mirror is one switch away.

## Which version do I take?

- **0.4.0** is for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer (the final shader API 0.2).
- **0.3.0** is for older builds that still serve shader API 0.1. The Nightly no longer loads it.
The launcher offers the one your game can run.

Original code, no Minecraft assets. Source: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders

versions.changelog:
Daybreak 0.4.0 is Daybreak 0.3.0 for Horizon's final shader API 0.2, for the Horizon Nightly of 2026-11-18 and newer. That Nightly no longer loads API 0.1 packs, Daybreak 0.3 and older among them.

- **Linear light and HDR.** API 0.2 hands every stage linear colours. Daybreak keeps its look by lighting and grading in the same space as before, bloom is filtered and added in linear light, and highlights above white are kept for HDR displays. Ported by Abeansits.
- **Final API 0.2 inputs.** Daybreak draws terrain from `shaded_tint` and finds the water's surface by its normal, so it stays off the terrain look storage that reading `tint`, `shade`, `ao` or `face` turns on (more terrain memory and a world reload when the pack starts).
- Everything 0.3.0 brought: coloured light only where it is coloured (fewer stutters), screen-space water reflections, sharper and cheaper shadows.

On the Nightly of 2026-11-13 and older, stay on Daybreak 0.3.0.

Release notes: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders/releases/tag/v0.4.0

projects.name: Dis-Enchanting Table
projects.summary: Move an item's enchantments onto a book for 25 experience points at a Dis-Enchanting Table.
projects.description:
A port of [Dis-Enchanting Table](https://github.com/Mods-For-Lupin/Dis-Enchanting-Redux) by Lupin and Jason13 for Horizon. The table strips enchantments off an item and writes them onto a book.

- Place the table and right-click it: put an enchanted item in the input slot, a `minecraft:book` in the book slot, and an empty slot for the result.
- A right click moves the enchantments onto a new enchanted book and costs 25 experience points; an enchanted book needs at least two enchantments to be worth dis-enchanting. A missing book, missing experience or an occupied output leaves everything as it was.
- The cost is paid **before** the result is granted: a level cost comes off immediately, a points cost is charged at the tick's end and the book is written only once the charge succeeded (a failed write refunds it), and a second take in the same tick cannot spend the same points twice.
- The book slot is validated as an actual `minecraft:book`, including the hopper path and a save reload, so no other item is consumed for an enchanted book.
- The table keeps the jar's light 7, its 12-pixel shape, its stone-pickaxe harvest level, and hoppers may fill the input and book slots.
- `/disenchanting_table info <x> <y> <z>` prints the three slots for testing.

Unlicense — the original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/disenchanting_table/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository.

projects.name: Dynamic FPS
projects.summary: Drops the frame rate while the window is in the background, so Horizon stops burning power for a screen nobody is looking at.
projects.description:
Alt-tabbing out of Horizon leaves it rendering as fast as it can into a window you cannot see. Dynamic FPS answers the game's own frame-rate hook and lowers the cap while the window is not the one in front.

- In the background: the cap you pick (1, 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 FPS), 10 by default.
- Minimised: 1, 5 or 10 FPS, 1 by default. Horizon already caps a minimised window at
  10 FPS before this mod's hook runs, so higher values would have no effect and are not
  offered.
- A lower cap you set yourself is never raised, and the game is never pushed below one
  frame, so input, ticks and the network keep running.
- Settings under Options > Mods > Dynamic FPS.

1 FPS is a power-saving trade-off, not a performance setting: at one frame per second the
client cannot keep up with a 20 TPS world. Ticks, chat and the network still run, but the
picture updates only once a second until the window is focused again; use 10 FPS if you
need the client to stay in step.

This is what Horizon's `framerate_limit` hook documents itself for, and what the game's Battery Mode uses. Nothing is drawn and nothing is sent: it only returns a number.

An independent MIT implementation that follows [Dynamic FPS](https://github.com/juliand665/Dynamic-FPS) by juliand665 (MIT) without copying its code; see the NOTICE in the source.

projects.name: Dynamic Trees
projects.summary: Dynamic Trees for Horizon, slice 1: an oak acorn grows through named stages into a full tree, and resumes after a relaunch.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Dynamic Trees 1.7.2](https://github.com/DynamicTreesTeam/DynamicTrees) by DynamicTreesTeam (**MIT**) — slice 1: the oak.

Dynamic Trees replaces vanilla tree growth with trees that grow procedurally over time. This slice carries one species: an **oak acorn** planted on soil grows through named stages — sprout, trunk, branches, canopy, mature — placing trunk, branches and leaves progressively, and resumes after a relaunch.

**Implemented so far**

- `dynamictrees:oak_seed` (the Oak Acorn) used on the top face of dirt-like soil plants `dynamictrees:oak_sapling`; stone and an occupied spot are refused and nothing is spent.
- Growth starts on the sapling's own random tick or a bone-meal click, then proceeds **over time**: one plan step per 20 server ticks, gated by upstream's `growth_rate` (seeded), with the trunk height derived from `signal_energy` and `lowest_branch_height`.
- The tree lives in a world-level record (`<save>/horizon-mod-data/dynamictrees/trees.tsv`), because a tree spans many positions and the pin reverts a block entity's writes inside its own tick; a world close flushes and forgets it, so trees cannot leak between worlds.
- `/dynamictrees info <pos>` and `/dynamictrees list` report the stage, the steps and the block counts.

**Not yet ported**

- **Every other species** (acacia, birch, cherry, dark oak, jungle, mangrove, spruce, crimson and the rest): each needs its own species numbers and shape.
- **The tree-pack API** is Java-only, so a Horizon port cannot host the add-on packs that depend on it.
- **The cell-kit solver** is not implemented — this plan honours the species' numbers, not the solver's geometry.
- **Rooty soil and fertility**, branch radius, tapering, stripping, rot and disease, fruit, voluntary seed drops, the falling-tree entity and leaf age-decay.
- **The dendro pouch, staff, potions, dirt bucket and config screens**, and worldgen replacement of vanilla trees.

Upstream's MIT notice travels inside the package. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the shared per-player sphere. Slice 1 gave each controller its own sphere because the old pin had no level saved data; at this pin the sphere is a dimension-scoped attachment, so receivers subscribe to a sphere named by the placing player's UUID, several receivers share one reservoir, and the store survives a save, a quit and a relaunch. projects.name: Earshot
projects.summary: Proximity voice chat for servers running Simple Voice Chat: 3D voices, push to talk, whisper and voice groups
projects.description:
Proximity voice chat for Horizon. Talk to the players near you on servers that run **Simple Voice Chat**: with Java players using Simple Voice Chat, and with other Horizon players using Earshot.

- **Proximity voice** with 3D audio: voices come from where players stand and fade with distance.
- **Push to talk** (Mouse 4), held or toggled, or **voice activation** with an adjustable threshold and a live mic level.
- A **mic test**: hear yourself as the others would.
- **Whisper** (Mouse 5, held): only players close by hear you.
- **Voice groups**: create one (normal, open or isolated, with an optional password), join one with a click; a panel lists the members and lights up whoever is talking.
- **Noise reduction**, **per-player volume**, **mute** and **deafen**.
- A **mic icon** on the HUD, and a **speaker icon** beside other players' name tags while they talk.
- Opus audio and AES-128-GCM encryption, as the server expects.

Keys: V opens the voice menu, M mutes, N deafens; rebind them in Controls. Mods > Earshot > Config has a voice chat switch and debug info.

**Network use:** when you join a server that runs Simple Voice Chat, Earshot asks it for a voice key over the game connection, then sends and receives encrypted voice over UDP to the address the server names (default port 24454). It contacts nothing else, and stays quiet on servers without Simple Voice Chat. From 2.0.6, muting closes the microphone within a moment (tested on Windows), and it is only opened while voice chat is on and you're not muted, once a server's voice session or the mic test needs it. Nothing is ever sent while you're muted. 2.0.4 and older keep the microphone open while muted.

**Platforms:** tested on Windows. macOS should work but is untested. On Linux the launcher refuses it: its audio library uses ALSA there, which the game links too.

Works with Simple Voice Chat 2.6.27 (compatibility version 20), Fabric and Paper. Hosting voice on a Horizon dedicated server is off in this version, until its game patch is tested again (horizon-rust/horizon#18462 is fixed).

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/earshot

Earshot is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Simple Voice Chat or its author. It contains no Simple Voice Chat code or assets; its protocol support was worked out from our own network captures (PROTOCOL.md). Opus by opus-rs (BSD-3-Clause).

versions.changelog: Earshot is now client-only, so you can join Horizon servers and friends' worlds that don't have it (2.0.6 and older were refused with "These mods are not on this server: earshot"). Its voice server part was already off. Nothing else changed.

Muting now closes the microphone within a moment (Windows stops listing it in use) while playback keeps going; switching Voice chat off closes both. Nothing is sent while you're muted. The mic test can't be started while muted or off. Mute release contributed by TheApple05 (selfmonoraque5/earshot#1). Built for Nightly 2026-11-21 f037744.

Built for Nightly 2026-11-21 f037744. Review follow-ups: the vendored Opus decoder no longer has its OPUS_TRACE_PLC debug file trace; at most 64 players are decoded at once, so a server can't make it start a decoder per invented speaker; corrected the licence paths and the vendoring note. The entry now says only Windows is tested.

First release on the Horizon registry: built on Horizon's mod API for Nightly 2026-11-19 5ef7734, and also builds on later Nightlies where the mod API it uses is unchanged (tested on 2026-11-20 0a875da). Fixes a crash report on every game exit on Windows.

projects.name: elevatorid
projects.summary: A Horizon port of elevatorid.
projects.description:
A port of [ElevatorMod](https://github.com/VsnGamer/ElevatorMod) by Vasco (VsnGamer) for Horizon — the coloured elevators.

**Implemented so far**

- All 16 coloured elevators, on the jar's block template and with its models, textures, recipes, tags and names.
- Jump-up and sneak-down teleport the player to the nearest elevator of the same colour above or below, with the jar's search range and same-colour rule.
- The block entity and its saved state, and the carried assets in one self-loading archive.

**Not yet ported / deviations**

- **Teleport motion:** the move goes through the pin's command path at the tick, the only teleport surface the API offers, so horizontal velocity is lost and upstream's sound and particles are not sent.
- **Input:** a raw jump key edge is unavailable; the jump is inferred from the player's body, with `player_jump` as the exact edge at this pin (issue-shaped gap: give `native_player_tick` the player's input, `on_ground`/jump flag).
- **Suffocation** is approximated with a full-collision block, so glass and leaves differ at the edges.
- **Not carried:** camouflage, the options GUI, the directional model/arrow/yaw, `resetPitch`, the XP cost, mob spawning and `config/elevatorid-server.toml`.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/elevatorid/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with ElevatorMod's `Copyright (c) 2016 Vasco`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the arrival view: the `facing` and `directional` states and the landing rule. A plain elevator keeps the player's yaw and pitch; a directional one turns them to the block's face and levels the pitch, which is upstream's own rule and was previously always passed through from the jump. Proven in game on the same block with only `directional` flipped: a plain ride lands at yaw 33 and pitch 40, and a directional ride at yaw 270 and pitch 0. This version also closes the parity rule's sharpest hole in the port: 32 recipe files had shipped and not one had ever been crafted, and a new phase crafts all 16 — the shaped white and the fifteen shapeless redyes — asserting each output and that its ingredients were consumed, with eight wool and no pearl as the control. Four harness facts are recorded: `ctl click-slot`/`screen`/`ui` need `--offscreen` and hang headless, `ctl state` puts the view under `.player.yaw`/`.pitch`, `ctl block` puts the state at `.state` and needs a tick after `setblock`, and a forwarded run can overwrite a fresh log with the far box's copy.
First release

projects.name: Emojiful
projects.summary: :short_name: in chat shows the emoji (Twemoji).
projects.description:
Type `:smile:`, `:thumbsup:`, `:flag-us:` or any of nearly 2,000 short names in chat, and the line shows the Twemoji emoji. Messages are sent as typed, so players without the mod see the codes. One package with the code and the emoji images; no resource pack needed.

**Differences from the original:** Emoji codes become images only in received chat lines, not on signs, books, names or in the chat box while typing. There are no completions while typing a `:name` and no emoji picker button. Emoji typed as characters are drawn by the game's own font, not as Twemoji. There are no Emojiful custom or GIF emoji, no datapack emoji and no profanity filter. A code split across text colours stays as text.

A port of [Emojiful](https://github.com/InnovativeOnlineIndustries/Emojiful) 4.2.0 by HorizonStudio (Innovative Online Industries), published under its licence, MIT. The original copyright and licence notices are kept in the file (LICENSE, NOTICE).

Emoji graphics: [Twemoji](https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji), Copyright 2020 Twitter, Inc and other contributors, and jdecked/twemoji contributors, licensed under CC-BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/; full text in LICENSE-GRAPHICS), taken from [iamcal/emoji-data](https://github.com/iamcal/emoji-data)'s sheet_twitter_32_clean.png (MIT). The images are cut into font sheets; they are otherwise unchanged. Short names from iamcal/emoji-data.

No Minecraft code is included.

versions.changelog: One native package with the code and the Twemoji font, built with the exact-build SDK dd67b76 on the mod API only. Replaces the retired .hnmod; the separate emojiful_twemoji pack is no longer needed.

projects.name: Ender Undertow
projects.summary: An Enderman behind an underground miner can lift them off the floor and blink them into a nearby cave.
projects.description:
In Overworld survival, mining stone or ore with an Enderman close behind you can trigger an eight-tick lift followed by a short teleport. Turning to face it or keeping a wall between you prevents the pickup.

The pack looks for solid ground, headroom and an adjacent walkable space, then checks the destination again before arrival. If the original Enderman moves away, the carry ends. Each pickup starts a two-minute cooldown. Modpack authors can tune the default one-in-eight chance with a scoreboard setting.


**Installing Ender Undertow on Horizon 26.3**

- **Ender Undertow** (this listing) — World data pack for the mining and teleport encounter. It works on its own.
- [Cinematic](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_cinematic) — Native mod for the camera turn, lowered hands and color fade. Install on the host and each participating client, then opt in with `/trigger eu.scene set 1`.
- [Resources](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_resources) — Client resource pack for the Gentleman’s voice and wardrobe and the lingering portal sound. Enable it in Resource Packs.
- [Focus](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/ender_undertow_focus) — Optional client shader for blur and warble during the cinematic. Select it in Shader Packs.

[Download all four in one ZIP and see installation instructions](https://michado.dk/projects/ender-undertow/#install).

versions.changelog: Adds Rift and Gentleman encounters, safe home and diamond overlook landings, and optional cinematic cues.

projects.name: enderio
projects.summary: A Horizon port of enderio.
projects.description:
A port of [Ender IO](https://github.com/Team-EnderIO/EnderIO) (Unlicense, by Team-EnderIO) for Horizon. This first slice is the **item conduit** and its network.

**Implemented so far**

- `enderio:conduit` (the `minecraft:stone` template: hardness 1.5, blast resistance 10, no occlusion, a 3 px core outline) with six boolean state properties — `down`, `up`, `north`, `south`, `west`, `east` — and a `multipart` blockstate that draws the 3 px core plus one 2 px arm per connected side. The block carries a self-drop loot table.
- Connections: a face connects to another `enderio:conduit` or to a block with an item container reachable from the touching side (the pin's `native_container_slots`, API 48). The connection state is recomputed when a neighbour changes.
- Per-side configuration (input / output / disabled), the network cycle that groups connected conduits, and item transfer along it, all through the hopper-rule helpers so a refused item stays where it is.
- `/enderio info|config` readout and configuration commands, with the carried texture, models, language and loot inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The item filters (extract and insert filter slots), the speed tiers (enhanced and vibrant item conduits), priority and dye channels.
- The conduit screen (menu, slots and toggles) and the redstone control.
- The bundle (several conduit types in one block), facades, the Yeta Wrench, and every other conduit family (energy, fluid, gas, me, redstone, dense, ender).
- The rest of Ender IO's machines and blocks.

Unlicense, like the original; the port's sources are released under the same public-domain dedication and the notice travels inside the archive.

versions.changelog: Per-side redstone control, the gap line 'the conduit screen ..., the redstone control'. The four upstream modes (never_active, active_with_signal, active_without_signal, always_active) are stored per side beside the insert/extract toggles and applied to extraction, read from the conduit's neighbour signal. A fresh conduit now extracts nothing until its control is set, which is what the jar does — slice 1 copied the toggle and ignored the gate. Proven in game: default control moves nothing for 45 ticks; active_with_signal moves a full stack only while a redstone block is above the conduit and stops when it is removed; active_without_signal is its mirror.
First release

projects.name: enderstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of enderstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [EnderStorage](https://github.com/chicken-bones/EnderStorage) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The ender chest, keyed by its three wool colours, with the mod's own model, texture, blockstate, recipe, loot table and language.
- Upstream keeps **one inventory per frequency** in a world-global manager and every chest with that frequency opens the same container. Horizon gives a mod block entity its own slots, so the port keeps the frequency store as the truth and mirrors it into each chest once per tick.
- The mirror is a **three-way merge on counts**: an untouched slot adopts the store, and a slot a chest changed is applied to the store as a **delta**, so two chests that each withdraw from one stack subtract twice and two that each insert add twice. A stack that no longer fits stays in the chest that inserted it rather than being destroyed.
- The store persists per world and survives a relaunch.

**Not yet ported**

- **The tank does not store fluid at this pin.** The block entity can declare fluid tanks, but a bucket emptied into one does not keep the fluid: the engine's own bucket path consumes the item before any mod hook can refuse it, and a `FluidTanks::insert` over `horizon:fluids` loses the write (a 1000 mB insert leaves 0 after the tick; 500 mB is kept once and the next 500 mB refused; 250 mB is not kept at all; and cancelling the bucket event — which the mod must do so a full tank never pours into the world — takes the write back with the event's transaction). So the tank accepts the click, reads empty, and never pours into the world; the in-game leg asserts exactly that, so a pin that keeps the fluid makes it fail. The measured table and the SDK symbols are in the port's `notes.md` under *Gap: the declared tank at 0b14f8a*.
- **The pouch is deferred.** A pouch opens the same inventory from an item; a mod item has no menu route at this pin.
- Personal (owned) frequencies, the lid animation and the custom renderer are not carried.
- A slot whose *item* is replaced on two chests in the same tick is a genuine tie: one slot holds one item, so the later edit wins and the other stack remains in its own chest.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2020 covers1624, ChickenBones, Christopher R. Thompson (Ecu)`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`.

versions.changelog: Two inventory-loss repairs. A stack of empty buckets now drains one bucket and keeps the rest of the stack, where the old path replaced the whole held slot with a single item and seven buckets vanished. And a tank placed on a stocked frequency no longer erases the shared fluid: the merged tank and the obligation to write it are one value, so the snapshot is only ever what the entity holds. A third defect surfaced while proving the first: the click path ran a second exchange on the already-swapped hand, duplicating a bucket, so the swap now happens in the bucket item phase where it belongs.

Carry-dialect repair: two recipes were in the 1.21.1 object ingredient form 26.3 rejects, so the ender chest and the tank could not be crafted at all. Converted to bare ids. Proven in game: `ender_chest` crafts with its ender pearl consumed and the grid emptied. Both loot tables were already in the 26.3 shape and are untouched.
Review fixes: sibling-mirror commit and reach-gated readout, hand exchange in the tank transaction, and the load-time double Part attach. The tank fluid gap at 0b14f8a is now measured and stated.

projects.name: End's Delight
projects.summary: End foods for Farmer's Delight: shulker, dragon and chorus dishes, the End Stove, knives (needs Farmer's Delight 0.5 or later).
projects.description:
End foods for Farmer's Delight: shulker, dragon, endermite and chorus dishes, the End Stove, three feasts, the dragon leg, the chorus fruit pie, the chorus succulent and four knives.

**Needs** [farmersdelight](https://playhorizon.dev/mods/farmersdelight) 0.5 or later installed too (declared as a dependency, so the game names it if it's missing). Its End Stove, feasts, sneak-teleporting foods, recipes and mob drops run on that package's code.

**Differences from the original:** The dragon tooth knife does no extra damage to End mobs. Enderman gristle teleports you like a chorus fruit, up to 16 blocks around, where the Java mod sends you higher with less fall damage. Teleporting foods have no cooldown afterwards. The chorus succulent gives the same light at every size.

A port of [End's Delight](https://github.com/FoggyHillside/End-s-Delight) refabricated-1.20.1-2.5 by FoggyHillside, published under its licence, MIT. The original copyright and licence notices are kept in the file (LICENSE, NOTICE).

Its textures, models and data come from the original mod. No Minecraft code is included.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, projectile kills: an arrow kill now fills the blood extractor the player carries, which the melee-only hook never could. The credit rule is one listener on the death itself, so a melee kill cannot be filled twice and the existing melee phase remains the regression guard. Proven with three counterfactuals in one run: a twenty-health zombie killed with thirty-two arrows leaves the extractor at five hundred and forty-one of five thousand, the previous package's bytes at the same kill leave it at zero, and a zombie killed by a skeleton's arrow, whose owner was read back as that skeleton, leaves it at zero as well. The hook named in our brief did not work for this and the reason is measured rather than guessed: the death-loot hook does name the player for a bow kill, but a write to the player's inventory made there is discarded, so the fill moved to the death hook where the write lands. A second engine fact came with it: a player switched from survival to creative stops keeping a death hook's inventory write, so the kill phases run in survival and the numbers say why, two hundred and sixty-six in creative from launch, five hundred and ninety-eight in survival, and zero after the switch.
