projects.name: laserbridges
projects.summary: A Horizon port of laserbridges.
projects.description:
A port of [Laser Bridges & Doors](https://github.com/Mars-The-Planet/Laser-Bridges-And-Doors) (MIT, by Mars) for Horizon. This first slice is the **laser sources and the beams they project**.

**Implemented so far**

- In scope: the four sources `laser_source_block`, `laser_source_fullblock`, `laser_fence_source_block` and `laser_fence_source_fullblock`, with the upstream state set (`face` × `facing` × `powered` × `color`) and their upstream outlines and powered outlines.
- The two beams `laser_block_powered` and `laser_fence_powered` (unbreakable, light 10, thin collidable plates) that the sources write and clear.
- Placement: the clicked face becomes `face` and the placer's direction `facing`, with the attached variants' sturdy-support requirement.
- The bridge generator: the beam's length, the blocks it cuts through, where an obstruction stops it, and shrinking back when a source is switched off or removed.
- Redstone-driven switching, the carried models, textures, sounds metadata, recipes, loot and language, and the source and beam blocks declared as one content pack inside the `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The two receivers (`laser_attached_receiver`, `laser_attached_receiver_fence`): their blocks, models, textures, lang and recipes, and their redstone output (the colour copy from the laser in front).
- Dyeing a source with a dye or from a dispenser.
- The `laserbridges:on`/`off` playback sounds.
- The `config/laserbridges.json` options (`max_length`, `blocks_cut_through_by_lasers`): the port uses upstream's defaults.
- A colour change mid-line strands the far cells — upstream's exact-state test, kept deliberately.
- Beam blocks are unbreakable like upstream (the bedrock template), so a beam has no drop and no break sound.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/laserbridges/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two receivers: the attached receiver and its fence variant now power on a laser and copy its colour, where slice 1 carried only the sources. A receiver lights the lamp above it and leaves the one behind it dark — upstream's signal-face rule — clears both when the beam goes, stays off when it faces away, does not power from an unpowered source in front, and reports light 0 or a per state like the attached sources do. The fence variant refuses the side a plain stone accepts. Proven in game: all twelve carried recipes craft with their ingredients consumed, both receivers and sources drop themselves on a survival break, and 168 declared states are accepted. One upstream defect is recorded and not reproduced: `IReceiverBlock.updateState` computes "is it looking into me?" from its own state, so its guard can never fire, and the port implements the effective rule instead. The colour tint stays a recorded client-side gap — the state and the signal are asserted, never a visual.
First release

projects.name: laserio
projects.summary: A Horizon port of laserio.
projects.description:
A port of [LaserIO](https://github.com/Direwolf20-MC/LaserIO) by Direwolf20-MC for Horizon — the nodes, the connectors and the item cards.

**Implemented so far**

- `laserio:laser_node` and `laserio:laser_connector`, the network they form through their faces, and one card per side saved in the node's block entity.
- The item card: `insert` (upstream's default) or `extract`, with its channel and amount, placed by right-clicking the node (consumed outside creative).
- After the level tick, each extract card whose 20-tick operation falls on this tick takes the first item type the source side offers — skipping empty earlier slots, so they cannot stall a network — and moves up to its amount into the network's inventories. No destination means no extraction, and a refused item stays in the target's remainder.
- `/laserio info` readout, and the carried blockstates, models, textures, recipes, loot, tags, langs and creative tab.
- The mutation commands (`card`, `remove`, `mode`, `rate`, `face`) are **operator-only** (level 2): the node screen is a gap, so they are an administrative surface rather than something every player may use on any node.

**Not yet ported**

- The node screen (card settings UI), so players cannot yet configure cards by hand.
- Fluid, energy and gas cards, the advanced/wireless connectors, the lasers' rendering, filters and the round-robin/channel modes beyond a single channel.
- The full recipe chain and the guide book.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/laserio/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, channels as routing: a card's channel now decides where its stacks go. Upstream hands a stack only to inserter cards on the same channel and takes nothing when none answers, so until now the port's channel was decorative — every insert endpoint in a network was a destination, and the mod's central routing rule was missing. The service and destination order now carry the channel, the card stores it, and `/laserio channel` sets it. Five carried recipes were dead and are fixed, with their second half: all five used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` ingredient form the pin rejects, and the `c:` tags they name exist in no target data, so even the right shape could not match — the port now declares the seven tags it needs. Proven in game: the five recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and a wrong pattern crafts nothing; a channel-3 extract card fills the channel-3 card 20/20 and leaves the channel-0 card at 0; moving that card to channel 5 makes the extract card take nothing while the source keeps 20; and returning it receives all 20.
First release

projects.name: little_big_redstone
projects.summary: A microchip block that runs redstone logic on its circuit board.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Little Big Redstone](https://github.com/Swedz/Little-Big-Redstone) (MIT, by **Swedz**) for Horizon. This first slice is **one microchip** with the mod's own AND scene — two input ports, a 2-input AND gate, one output port and three wires.

**Implemented so far**

- **The microchip block.** The jar makes the microchip the *block* and the logic components *items on its circuit board*, so the slice is a placed microchip that holds a circuit: two input ports, a 2-input AND gate, one output port and three wires, saved in the block entity.
- **The guide's own scene runs in game:** inputs `0,0`, `0,1` and `1,0` leave the lamp dark and `1,1` lights it, with the per-face redstone properties tracking the ports.
- **Analog input:** A=15 with B=5 (a wire line decaying to `power=5`) still lights it, and the saved `microchip.power` reads 15.
- **State survives a quit and relaunch**, the circuit is inspectable and resettable with `/lbr circuit <x> <y> <z> status|clear|and`, and a signal arriving on a wire strongly powers what sits beside it.
- **Crafting** follows the jar's shaped recipes (circuit board plus the mod's tags), and the block drops itself to a pickaxe.

**Not yet ported**

- the other 15 microchip components and the guide's remaining scenes;
- the in-game guide book and the microchip's GUI (this slice configures with a command instead);
- the mod's own wire-rendering template (the slice uses a vanilla wire model).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the six-gate logic family: OR, XOR, NAND, NOR and NOT beside the existing AND. Each gate carries its own rule from the jar's own guide — OR and XOR are analog with XOR's odd parity, NOT/NAND/NOR are boolean, every gate takes 2 to 10 inputs clamped and NOT exactly 1 — and each has its saved compound type with `input_count`. A `/lbr circuit` action drives an output port so the guide's analog rule is observable in game. Proven in game: the truth tables per gate, analog 3+5 reading 5, XOR four-input parity (2 then 4 then 3 then 2 then 1 inputs), NAND `15,0` reading 1, NOR `0,0` reading 1, the `status` readout naming a gate and its input count, and refusals that leave the circuit unchanged.
First release

projects.name: Living Camera
projects.summary: A camera that moves with you: it leans into strafes, sways on turns, dips on landing and bobs with your steps
projects.description:
A camera that moves with you. It leans into strafes, tips as you jump and fall, sways on fast turns, dips when you land, bobs with your steps and breathes while you stand still. Everything runs on springs, so the camera eases into each motion and settles back with a little weight instead of snapping.

- **Strafe and forward lean**: the camera rolls into sideways movement and tips slightly while running.
- **Turn sway**: fast mouse turns tilt the view.
- **Jump and fall tilt**: the view lifts going up and dips coming down.
- **Landing dip**: a hard landing bumps the camera down, then it springs back.
- **Step bob**: a soft bounce in step with your walking, on top of vanilla's.
- **Idle breathing** and **Speed FOV** (off by default).
- **Hand sway**: the held item lags behind fast turns and leans with the camera.
- **Presets** (Subtle, Default, Cinematic, PvP), **damage shake**, and calmer effects **while aiming** or **riding mounts**.

Every effect has its own strength, plus overall intensity, smoothness and bounce presets. All in Mods > Living Camera > Config, with a key to toggle it in game.

Client side only: it works in single player and on any server. It uses only the mod API's hooks, with no game patches, no network and no file access beyond its own settings.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/living-camera

Inspired by Camera Overhaul by Mirsario (https://github.com/Mirsario/Minecraft-CameraOverhaul). Written from scratch for Horizon: it contains none of Camera Overhaul's code or assets and is not made or endorsed by Mirsario.

versions.changelog: Rebuilt on Horizon's new mod API (the .hmod SDK) for Nightly 2026-11-19 f00125f. Same effects and presets; settings now open from Mods > Living Camera > Config and start from the defaults once.

projects.name: Lumina
projects.summary: High performance with real-time shadows, physical water, roof overhang occlusion, volumetric 3D clouds, and sharp anti-aliasing
projects.description:
Native shaders designed for high frame rates and clean, balanced visuals without post-processing blur. All options are fully configurable directly in the shader settings menu.

**Lighting & Overhang Shading**
- Balanced daytime lighting with warm sun and clean azure shadows.
- Directional sky dome occlusion: accurate contrast between ground, walls, and ceilings.
- Non-linear ambient occlusion under house roofs, eaves, porches, and balconies.
- Selective midtone vibrance on grass and foliage without clipping bright highlights.
- Foliage subsurface scattering and sun-facing rim lighting.

**Shadows**
- Real-time sun and moon shadow maps with distortion-aware filtering.
- Acne-free shadows on terrain, blocks, and thin grass at any distance.
- Selectable shadow map resolution: 512, 1024, 1536, or 2048.

**Clarity Anti-Aliasing (FXAA)**
- Edge-selective geometric smoothing on block silhouettes, roofs, and stairs.
- Flat surfaces, textures, wood, stone, and UI remain 100% sharp with zero blurring.
- Modes: Sharp, Smooth, or Off.

**Water & Underwater**
- High-speed Screen Space Reflections (SSR) combined with planar mirror reflections.
- Physics-based Beer-Lambert light absorption with depth-dependent color transition.
- Snell's window when looking up from underwater with total internal reflection.
- Animated seabed caustics, wave refraction, and underwater depth fog.

**Clouds & Atmosphere**
- Raymarched procedural 3D cumulus clouds with Fast, Balanced, and Cinematic presets.
- Volumetric god rays through terrain and trees.
- Procedural rain puddles on grass and dirt with raindrop impact ripples.
- Custom weather rendering for rain and snow particles.
- Native block emission and dynamic colored lighting support.

**Setup Note:**
Set Clouds to OFF in your video settings to let the custom 3D clouds render properly.

projects.name: Map Preview
projects.summary: See a map's picture in its tooltip and in its inventory slot, so you can tell your maps apart
projects.description:
See what's on a map without holding it.

- **Tooltip preview**: hover a filled map and its picture shows in the tooltip. Always, or only while holding Shift, in three sizes, on paper or on the map background.
- **Slot preview**: every map in your hotbar, inventory and chests shows a small copy of its picture: as a full slot, with a border, or inside the map item's own frame.
- **Locked maps** get a glass rim, taken from your resource pack's glass texture.
- Frames follow your resource pack's map textures at any resolution, and maps update live as you explore.

All in Mods > Map Preview > Config.

Client side only: it works in single player and on any server. A preview needs the map's picture on your client: the server sends it for maps you carry, as vanilla does, so a map you've never carried may show no preview until you pick it up once.

The mod API doesn't show a client mod a map's pixels, so besides the mod API this mod patches one game function (input_hud_begin) to read the game's own map data and palette. It works on the Horizon build it is made for.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/map-preview

The map frame, glass and background modes were contributed by FitchWorks. Inspired by Map Tooltip by VendoAU (https://modrinth.com/mod/map-tooltip) and Map In Slot by Crec0 (https://modrinth.com/mod/map-in-slot). Written from scratch for Horizon: it contains none of their code or assets and is not made or endorsed by them.

versions.changelog: Much lighter slot pictures: matching rows merge into one shape, each map's slot picture is kept instead of rebuilt every frame, and "High" draws 32 x 32 cells (with 34 maps in the inventory: about 45 FPS instead of 22). Tooltips no longer flicker when moving between maps, and the ID line no longer touches the picture. Contributed by FitchWorks (selfmonoraque5/map-preview#3). Built for Nightly 2026-11-21 f037744.

Built for Nightly 2026-11-21 f037744. A "High" slot picture now draws at most 64 x 64 cells instead of 128 x 128 (no visible difference up to GUI scale 4, a quarter of the work), and the tooltip picture is only drawn for a map this mod reserved tooltip space for.

Rebuilt on Horizon's new mod API (the .hmod SDK) for Nightly 2026-11-19 5ef7734, with its game patches checked for that build. Settings now open from Mods > Map Preview > Config and start from the defaults once.

projects.name: measurements
projects.summary: A Horizon port of measurements.
projects.description:
A port of [Measurements](https://github.com/Mrbysco/Measurements) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The item `measurements:tape_measure`: right-click a block to place point A, right-click again to place point B and finish the measurement. The action bar shows `Distance: <d> blocks (X: <dx>, Y: <dy>, Z: <dz>)`.
- The distance is Euclidean over the coordinate differences, printed with one decimal (`5.0`, `7.1`, `0.0`), with the deltas as integers.
- The next click starts a new point A; shift-right-click removes the latest measurement (`Measurement undone (N left)`, or `Measurement cleared`).
- The same block twice reports `Distance: 0.0 blocks (X: 0, Y: 0, Z: 0)`.
- A session is dropped when the tape leaves the main hand, when the player changes dimension, and one tick after a player leaves.

**Not yet ported**

- **Delivery is the action bar, not an in-world box.** Upstream is a client-only renderer (`MeasurementBox` draws an AABB and three axis labels); it has no chat/action-bar readout and no Euclidean distance. The pin has no client render hook usable in the headless harness, so the port reports through `native_action_bar`. Deferred: the drawn box, its colours, text size, line width and the live crosshair preview.
- **The port prints the Euclidean distance (one decimal) and coordinate differences**, where upstream's labels are inclusive block counts (`|Δ|+1`): the same 0→5 measurement reads 5 here and 6 in upstream's label.
- One process-wide client list upstream becomes per-player sessions here, pruned one tick after a player leaves (the pin has no quit hook).
- The "still holding" reset checks the main hand only; an off-hand-only tape can start a measurement and is cleared on the next player tick.
- The recipe is accepted by `horizon-mod check` with the supplied `#c:ingots/iron` tag, but the harness did not craft it in game.

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

A port of [Mekanism](https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism) by Aidan C. Brady and the Mekanism contributors for Horizon. These first slices bring four pieces of the ore-processing chain:

- **Energized Smelter** — 50 FE/t, 200 ticks per smelt, a 20,000 FE buffer.
- **Enrichment Chamber** — the jar's recipes: one ore becomes two dusts, raw ore 3 becomes 4, a raw block 1 becomes 12.
- **Basic Energy Cube** — a 4,000,000 FE buffer.

Feed items and FE through their sides and right-click a machine to open its menu.

**Not yet ported**

- **The four block recipes are this slice's own**, using vanilla stand-ins (iron, redstone, glass, copper) for the steel casing, the basic alloy, the circuits and the energy tablet that this slice does not register; upstream's recipes depend on the steel chain, which is a later slice.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2017-2025 Aidan C. Brady`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 8, the chemical washer: the port's first fluid machine, where a dirty slurry and five millibuckets of water become a clean one. The question the brief asked is answered before the build and it is the opposite of the chemical one: the pin's fluid capability is a shared resource type, so unlike a mod's own chemical it crosses packages and a real tank answers through the declared handler — inserted ten thousand, saved, and read back attributed to the game rather than to the mod. The numbers are the jar's own, re-read for this machine rather than carried from its siblings: two hundred FE a tick, eighty thousand of buffer, two hundred ticks, ten thousand of each tank, and the water and slurry spent at the finish rather than per tick, which a mid-operation read confirms by still holding all thousand. Proven in game with one operation charged exactly and the rest of the brief's figures kept: the buffer empties, the output holds one clean iron, the water tank sits at nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-five, the machine's input is empty, and the neighbour tank falls by the unit it is about to spend. All seven washing rows sweep, and the fluid and chemical worlds are kept apart both ways: water is unknown to the chemical handler and there is no fluid handler where the chemical one lives.

Slice 7, the basic factory family: five machines that run the same recipe three times side by side, one input and output pair per process, sharing a buffer and, for the two gas machines, one tank. Every number was re-read for this family rather than carried from its single-machine sibling, including the buffer formula that multiplies by the process count, which gives thirty thousand for the three-item factories, a hundred and twenty thousand for purification and two hundred and forty thousand for injection, and a gas tank of two hundred and ten per process. Proven in game: three iron ore in three processes make nine clumps and empty both the buffer and three ticks of gas per process, while one ore in one process makes three; forty thousand FE charges exactly two hundred ticks without finishing an operation, which is the shared buffer being paid per working process; and the item factories take three ore to three ingots with the buffer emptied. A real defect surfaced that the unit tests had not caught: the factory drew its neighbour's gas while unpowered, so the gas ask now counts only the processes the tick can pay for and is pinned by two tests.

Slice 6, the purification chamber: the middle of the ore chain, where a raw ore and oxygen become three clumps. It is the same machine shape as the injection chamber but its numbers are its own, read rather than carried over: two hundred FE a tick rather than four hundred, eighty thousand of buffer, and a whole operation is forty thousand. Proven in game with three counterfactuals in one run: four thousand oxygen in a tank turns one iron ore into three clumps for exactly forty thousand FE and leaves the tank at three thousand eight hundred, which is the per-tick draw times two hundred; with no tank beside it the chamber sits full and the ore untouched; with a hydrogen chloride tank, which is the injection chamber's gas, nothing moves and the tank is untouched. The chain is proved end to end as the data declares it rather than as our brief guessed: the clump crushes to a dirty dust and the dirty dust enriches to a dust in the enrichment chamber, while this chamber given a dirty dust sits at eighty thousand FE with an untouched input, which is the counterfactual that proves the two machines are not interchangeable. Fifteen purification rows ran, and the crusher and injecting sweeps still pass at a hundred and forty-eight and seventy-two.

Slice 5, the chemical injection chamber: the consumer half of the capability slice 4 published, so a machine now pulls gas out of a neighbour's tank through the key on its tick and turns ore into shards with it. Two numbers were read from the artefact rather than assumed: the raw iron row wants hydrogen chloride and not hydrogen, which makes hydrogen a useful wrong-gas control, and this machine costs four hundred FE a tick rather than the fifty of its siblings, so an operation is eighty thousand, and the cell draws one tick's gas two hundred times, so a whole operation empties two hundred times the per-tick amount. Proven in game with three counterfactuals in the same run: a tank of four thousand hydrogen chloride turns three raw iron into eight shards and ends at three thousand eight hundred, which is exactly two hundred times the row's per-tick; with no tank beside it the chamber sits at zero progress with its energy untouched; a tank of oxygen behaves the same; and a hydrogen tank is left alone. All seventy-two carried rows ran, and each drew exactly its own per-tick amount from the tank, which is the assertion that would fail if the pull were inert. The limit found in slice 4 holds and is recorded rather than worked around: the provider and the consumer here are the same crate's tank and chemical type, which is why this draw resolves.

Slice 4, the chemical capability: one resource, one published capability key, one block entity holding a tank and one item that carries a chemical. A basic chemical tank holds sixty-four thousand units and names them in its own saved data, and a gauge dropper takes two hundred and fifty units a call into its component, so a chemical can now be moved between a machine and a hand the same way items and energy are. Proven in game in five parts: the capability is published by name and lists Mekanism's thirty-two chemicals with hydrogen among them; an insert of four thousand units lands in the tank and reads back from the block data as the id and the number exactly; a partial drain takes two hundred and fifty of a thousand asked, leaving three thousand seven hundred and fifty in the tank and putting exactly two hundred and fifty on the item; an unknown chemical is refused by name and moves nothing; and the counterfactual against a block entity that answers items and energy but not this key finds no handler and no saved chemical. This is the surface two stopped add-ons were waiting for: the article of Mekanism's identity that this port had none of, noted in its own manifest as a gap for four slices.

Slice 3, the Crusher — the ore-processing machine that needs no new capability: 50 FE/t, a 20,000 FE buffer and 200 ticks (10,000 FE) per operation, from the jar's own config, carrying 145 of its 313 crushing rows (the rest need dusts this port does not register, and each skipped row is printed by the generator). Two defects found while carrying it, both fixed. First: every shaped recipe in 0.2.x used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` ingredient form, which 26.3 rejects — all four existing recipes and the new one could not craft at all; they now use bare item ids and are proven in game. Second: the local `Stack` and `Recipe` types shadowed SDK names, so the `uses` table claimed SDK types the port never used and `fits` against a different build failed; renamed `ItemAmount` and `MachineRecipe`, and the table is now true. Proven in game: cobblestone becomes gravel with the buffer at 0 after exactly one 10,000 FE operation, all 145 rows crush in a sweep, an uncharged crusher does nothing, and dirt with no recipe burns nothing.
First release

projects.name: Mekanism: Generators
projects.summary: Heat generator and the graphite/lava energy chain from Mekanism: Generators, with the jar's burn times and FE rates.
projects.description:
A port of [Mekanism: Generators](https://github.com/mekanism/Mekanism) (MIT, by Aidan C. Brady and the Mekanism contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **heat generator** and the graphite/lava energy chain behind it.

**Implemented so far**

- `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator`, a fuel slot (container slot 0) that takes any item with a furnace burn time and turns one item a tick into `burnTime / 20` mB of lava: coal 80 mB, a lava bucket 1,000 mB, and a crafting remainder replaces the stack.
- A 24,000 mB lava tank (this port's saved int `lava`; upstream's fluid capability is not declared in this slice, so only the fuel slot fills it).
- A heat capacitor of 10 units, fed by 200 heat/t while lava burns, 30 per lava side and 100 in the Nether, cooled by the 0.5 thermal-efficiency factor, so the capacitor settles at its stable temperature and the generator reports 100 % efficiency.
- The generator's FE buffer (160,000 FE, output only at up to 1,020 FE/t) declared as the block's energy capability, so another mod's cable can read and drain it.
- `/mekanismgenerators info|energy` readout, plus the carried block model, texture and language entries, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- No FE *output* into a neighbour: the generator fills its buffer and declares the capability, but nothing pushes it outward. The API-142 transfer helpers exist at this pin, so a cable slice can add it.
- No fluid capability: the tank is a saved int, so a pipe cannot fill it and nothing reads it as lava.
- No GUI: fuel goes in through the container, and state is read with the command.
- No `active` block state, so the `heat_generator_active` model, the sound that goes with it and the block's animation are not carried.
- The other generators (gas-burning, bio, solar, wind, advanced solar, laser, fusion, turbine), the generator upgrades and the boiler are later slices.

MIT; the upstream copyright line (2017-2025 Aidan C. Brady) and the full permission notice travel inside the archive at `mixins/mekanismgenerators/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, energy output: the heat generator now pushes its buffer into the block on the face its state names, which is the half of the tick that was missing — it filled its own buffer and nothing ever left. Upstream's rule is the one carried: emit to the front face only, up to twice the production rate, taking only what that neighbour accepts, inside one transaction. Proven in game on a two-mod game with our own mekanism parent: the generator held 56,432 FE and the cube on its facing face went 15,300 to 71,888 while the generator fell to zero, the cube on the opposite face stayed at zero, the steady rate measured 12,096 FE over about a hundred ticks, and with the front cube removed the generator stored 11,984 itself. The red leg is the same scenario with the emit call removed: the buffered FE did not reach the front cube, plus nothing. One thing is recorded rather than claimed: the carried recipe stays `blocked(no c:ingots/osmium provider)` because the game rejects its tag, so it is not counted as crafted. The slice also fixed its own repin properly — the manifest bump alone leaves the old SDK in `.horizon/sdk`, which is now a documented trap.

**Not yet ported**

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the recycling factory at every tier the jar registers: advanced, elite and ultimate beside the basic one, each with its own process count, energy buffer and container. The buffer is the jar's own formula — half the machine's storage or its usage, whichever is larger, times the tier's processes — giving 30,000, 50,000, 70,000 and 90,000 FE, which corrects slice 1's figure of 20,000 for the basic factory: that was a single machine's storage, not a factory's. The five extra tiers the mod names are recorded `blocked(evolvedmekanism-not-ported)` rather than faked, because the jar appends them only when Evolved Mekanism is loaded and it is not in the registry. Proven in game: each tier stalls at its own process count on 10,000 FE — advanced at forty units five times, elite at twenty-nine three times and twenty-eight four times, ultimate at twenty-three twice and twenty-two seven times — then finishes every process on exactly the energy it had left with one scrap each and a zero buffer; the four containers open nine, eighteen, eighteen and twenty-seven slots; and a survival break drops the ultimate factory beside a vanilla stone break as the differential. The tier roll measured the real seventeen percent, which the scenario had only pinned for the basic tier.
First release

projects.name: Menu Panorama
projects.summary: Put your own wallpaper behind the main menu in Horizon — Minecraft 26.3, rewritten in Rust.
projects.description:
Menu Panorama is a resource pack for **Horizon** — Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten from scratch in **Rust**.

It replaces the six textures of the main-menu background with a picture you choose. It is a plain resource pack, not a Java mod: no mod loader, no Java, and no code from the pack is executed. Horizon loads it natively.

- **Any photo** in the `room` mode: the picture is shown whole on the four walls, with mirrored seams and soft colours above and below.
- **A 360° equirectangular panorama** in the `360` mode: the sphere is cut into six cube faces, so the view stays seamless when the camera turns.
- **Auto** picks the mode from the image's aspect ratio.

Build a pack in the browser with `panorama-maker.html`: drop an image, choose a face size, download the `.zip`. Everything runs locally; the picture never leaves the computer. `make_panorama.py` does the same from the command line.

The pack only changes `assets/minecraft/textures/gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png`; gameplay, sounds and other textures are untouched. `pack.mcmeta` is made for Horizon 26.3 (resource format 97) and also declares formats 15–999, so the same file loads in Minecraft Java 1.21+. A demo pack is attached to every release.

MIT licensed. Source, the browser generator and the CLI are in the repository.

versions.changelog:
First release.

- Demo sunset pack: six 1024×1024 faces and a 128×128 icon.
- `panorama-maker.html`: browser generator with drag & drop, auto/room/360 modes and 512/1024/2048 face sizes.
- `make_panorama.py`: CLI with the same modes, preview output and `--description`.
- `pack.mcmeta` for Horizon 26.3: resource format 97, `pack_format` 34, formats 15–999.
- MIT licence.

projects.name: minecolonies
projects.summary: A town hall founds a colony, a citizen joins and farms it — with generated art.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [MineColonies](https://github.com/ldtteam/minecolonies) (GPL-3.0 code; the mod's own art is All Rights Reserved, so **every asset here is generated by this port**) for Horizon. This first slice is **a town hall, a colony, one citizen and one job**.

**Implemented so far**

- **Founding:** placing a `minecolonies:blockhuttownhall` founds a colony with a default name (`<owner>'s Colony`), its owner, centre, a **64-block (4-chunk) radius**, the founding tick and its records of citizens and harvests. Legality is decided before the block appears, so an illegal hall never exists.
- **Refusals that matter:** a second hall too close is refused, a hall **120 blocks across and 120 up** is refused (founding distance is horizontal — the colony is a 2D claim), and a second colony for the same owner is refused.
- **A citizen and a job:** `/minecolonies citizen hire|list`, `/minecolonies job assign <citizen> farmer|info` and `/minecolonies colony info|rename|radius`. The farmer needs a `minecolonies:blockhutfarmer` in the colony, walks to a mature wheat every 40 ticks, harvests it, replants at age 0 and counts it; a citizen with no colony does nothing.
- **Everything survives a quit and relaunch** — name, roster, radius and harvest count are in the town hall's saved data.
- **The art is generated**, never copied: `tools/gen_assets.py` builds all 15 asset files from a named 10-colour palette and three model templates, and regenerating gives byte-identical files.

**Not yet ported**

- the other ~40 jobs, the builder and its schematics, the research tree, and the colony/citizen UI (the commands above are the surface);
- happiness, saturation, requests, raids, building-driven growth and worldgen colonies;
- the citizen's own renderer (its texture is generated but not yet bound), and the proper hut and scythe shapes.

**Licence.** MineColonies' code is **GPL-3.0**; its art is **All Rights Reserved**, so this port ships **regenerated art only** and contains no upstream texture, model or language file. The GPL-3.0 text and a notice naming the authors, the upstream URL and the exact jar with its sha256 travel inside the archive; the port is a derivative of the code under the same licence with its complete source published.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 9f42064 and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the two job buildings: a lumberjack's hut and a mine, so the two jobs added last time now have the building their own rule expects, and a citizen cannot be assigned a job whose building is missing. One marker type names the building, which is what lets one query answer for every job instead of special-casing the farmer. Proven in game with the refusal as the boundary: assigning a lumberjack with no hut is refused with a message naming the block and the colony, the same citizen then leaves a whole four-log tree standing over two hundred ticks, and with the hut placed the same tree falls to four logs in the chest with a sapling left on the stump; job info reads the hut present, and after the hut is broken in survival with an iron axe, which is needed because a creative break drops nothing, the drop is the hut itself and job info reads missing. The mine works the same way for the miner, whose shaft is one by one and eight deep with the bedrock untouched. Both recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and a wrong grid crafts nothing. The licence half is measured rather than asserted: all twenty-five asset files were hashed against all twenty-two thousand seven hundred and forty-seven entries in the jar, and none matched, with the generator re-rendering every one byte-identically.

projects.name: Minimap, Worldmap and waypoints reworked
projects.summary: An adaptive minimap and world map with named waypoints, portals, world borders and a biome readout.
projects.description:
An adaptive minimap and a full world map for Horizon, with a persistent per-world terrain cache.

- Minimap in four corners, square or round, 64–256 GUI pixels, 0.1–4 blocks per pixel, and optional player rotation.
- Player arrow on both maps shows the viewing direction and accounts for minimap rotation.
- English, Russian, French, Spanish and German interfaces follow the game language, including regional variants.
- World map opened by a rebindable key (M by default); drag to pan and scroll to zoom under the cursor, with eased camera motion.
- Independent dimension selection for the minimap and the world map (Player / Overworld / Nether / End), without teleporting the player.
- Hover shows the pointed-at coordinates, the localised biome and waypoint names; the hovered block is outlined.
- Right-click menu: copy coordinates, create a named waypoint, or teleport when the client knows the player has game-master permission.
- Configurable two-letter initials distinguish waypoints sharing their first letter: similar colours (default), any colours, or a single letter; the same labels appear on maps, in the list and in 3D.
- Separate waypoint manager (N by default) for creating, renaming and deleting waypoints; waypoints are drawn as first-letter markers on the HUD through walls and on both maps.
- 3D-world waypoint markers in the waypoint's colour (or a skull for deaths), through walls; the label can be letter + distance, letter only, or name + distance, and can be shown only while the crosshair is on the marker. Each point can hide its own 3D marker.
- Death waypoints are placed automatically as numbered black skulls and can be removed on approach or switched off in the settings.
- Eight compass direction letters (localised) or the game's axis names at the inner edge of both maps, tracking true north.
- Water and glass-family blocks are semi-transparent, water tint thickens with depth, grass-like ground cover is skipped, and flowers/crops use their real colours.
- Portals (Nether, End and End gateways) are marked and show their destination; Nether destinations prefer the nearest known portal, otherwise coordinate conversion.
- Overworld and Nether world borders are drawn on both maps (the Nether border is scaled to the same physical area).
- Relief shading crosses chunk borders; unknown terrain is transparent; the minimap renders at high resolution for smooth movement.
- Settings and named waypoints persist asynchronously in the mod data folder. Waypoints are isolated by save/server identity and dimension, with 64 points per world/server. Legacy unscoped points are deleted on upgrade; preferences are retained.
- Both maps stream reusable GPU tile pages. Persistent world-space overview tiles accelerate distant views; camera and zoom targets are prefetched, retaining coarse coverage until finer tiles are ready. Detailed terrain preserves original block texels when zoomed in. Detailed and LOD terrain, sampled heights, biome names and portals persist across reconnects and restarts in one `.mwwr` container per single-player save/server address. A **Map RAM** slider (16–512 MiB, default 64 MiB) budgets retained terrain; no network requests are made by the mod.
- Each of the 67 vanilla biomes has an individual 16×16 icon. Waypoint colours can be edited, and Show on map centres the world map on a selected waypoint.
- World, actual-render/LOD and chunk-render borders have hover labels; right-click outlines the selected chunk and region.

- Map caches lists world/server names and available local icons, file sizes and compatibility. View saved terrain and player position, switch saved layers, manage waypoints or move to coordinates from the main menu. Confirm deletion of idle caches or rebuild derived images while retaining saved terrain.
- Distant terrain uses snow-aware climate/height approximation, fixed world-space biome blending and shared water opacity: snowy taiga and mangrove water retain their expected appearance. Detailed terrain remains authoritative; fresh LOD samples gradually refresh legacy colours.
- Version 0.7.9 is a flat source .hmod for the signed native SDK, pinned to Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da), Minecraft 26.3 and SDK Rust 1.99.1. Existing scoped waypoints, settings and terrain containers remain in use.

Created by daniliammo and continued by Gurov08ruS after the original account was removed from GitHub.

The runtime uses only portable standard-library APIs and is intended for Linux, macOS and Windows. The 0.7.0 SDK port was built and tested in a live Linux game; macOS and Windows runs remain unverified.

versions.changelog: Offline cache maps with progressive terrain loading, saved Nether layers and waypoint editing. Safe cache deletion, retry after a busy lease, release on disconnect, and title Options and controller routing. Adds coloured icons and precise waypoint teleport. Requires Nightly 2026-11-20 (0a875da).

Since 0.6.0: signed native SDK and .hmod migration; faster distant LOD and persistent overview/GPU tile streaming; asynchronous cache manager with world/server identities and safe image rebuilding; snow/ice and mangrove-water LOD fixes; configurable two-letter waypoint labels on maps and in 3D. Preserves scoped waypoints, settings and canonical terrain. Requires Nightly 2026-11-18 (0b14f8a). Compression and canonical conversion remain future work.

projects.name: modern_industrialization
projects.summary: A Horizon port of modern_industrialization.
projects.description:
A port of [Modern Industrialization](https://github.com/AztechMC/Modern-Industrialization) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- `modern_industrialization:electric_macerator`, one block: a **32,000 FE buffer** that any face may fill and nothing may drain (upstream's `EnergyComponent.buildInsertable` is insert-only). The mod's own default is 1 EU = 10 FE, so 3,200 EU = 32,000 FE.
- One item input slot and four item output slots: hoppers insert into slot 0 and pull from slots 1..=4.
- `CrafterComponent`'s tick in the pure runtime: a run starts when the buffer covers the recipe, is consumed at the machine's EU rate, and overclocks by the mod's own divisor.
- The jar's macerator recipes that only need vanilla materials, with tag inputs resolved to the vanilla items the tags hold.
- `/modern_industrialization info|energy|efficiency` (upstream has no commands).

**Not yet ported**

- **No crafting recipe** for the machine or the dusts: the creative tab is the entry point, and the four block recipes are the port's own, using vanilla stand-ins (iron, redstone, glass) until the steel chain, the basic alloy and the circuits this slice does not carry arrive.
- **34 of the jar's 324 macerator recipes** are carried. The other 290-odd need MI's own ingots, plates, gears, rods and wires, which this slice does not register.
- **No data-driven recipe type**: the pin offers no machine-recipe registry for a native mod, so the table is a `const` in `runtime.rs`; adding a recipe is a code change.
- No menu: `ModContainer` has no per-slot rule for a player's menu at this pin, so the machine is driven by hoppers.
- The energy and efficiency commands refuse any block entity that is not this macerator, and the energy hook leaves another mod's declaration for the same block alone.

MIT: the original copyright (`Copyright (c) 2020 Azercoco & Technici4n`) and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, the energy hatches: ten blocks, five tiers each way, an input and an output, so a multiblock can finally be fed electricity through its shell instead of only through its controller. The tiers are the jar's own, thirty-two EU up to a hundred and twenty-eight million, and their buffers follow; the superconductor tier's real buffer exceeds what this pin can hold, so it is declared at the largest value a thirty-two-bit buffer can express and the difference is stated rather than hidden. Proven in game in the way that matters for a hatch: five thousand FE put into the hatch appears in the controller's buffer and leaves the hatch, a run of exactly twelve thousand makes one coke with both ending at zero, and a run of eleven thousand nine hundred and eighty stalls at nine hundred and ninety-eight of a thousand with the same recipe and no product, which is the differential that shows the energy came from the hatch rather than from nowhere. Each tier clamps at its own capacity when filled twice over, and an output hatch drains the controller back out. The shell accepts the hatch in place of a brick and refuses it in the middle ring. The item and fluid hatches from the last slice still pass, and the coke oven's own recipe list is unchanged as a regression.
First release

projects.name: Modern Dynamics
projects.summary: The item pipe and extractor attachment: 4 items every 40 ticks between inventories, ported.

A port of [Modern Dynamics](https://github.com/Technici4n/Modern-Dynamics) by Technici4n for

Implemented so far

- `moderndynamics:extractor`, placed on a pipe side by right-clicking with the item (consumed outside creative) or by `/moderndynamics attach`; the side is saved with the block entity.

- The jar's recipes and carried content, the `/moderndynamics info` readout, and persistence across a relaunch.

Not yet ported

- the fluid pipe, the five energy cables (LV/MV/HV/EV/superconductor) and the machine extender;
- the attractor, filter and inhibitor attachments, the wrench, the attachment screen and the upgrade data;

projects.description:
A port of [Modular Routers](https://github.com/desht/ModularRouters) by Des Herriott (desht) for Horizon — the Router, the Puller Mk1 and the Sender Mk1.

**Implemented so far**

- `modularrouters:modular_router`: nine module slots and five upgrade slots saved in the block entity, its facing, the `active` block state while a module works, and its one-slot buffer exposed as the block's item container on all six faces.
- Two modules: the **Puller Mk1** takes from the container beside the router into the buffer, topping up a buffer stack of the same resource first and never more than the Stack Upgrade count or the room left; the **Sender Mk1** pushes from the buffer into the first container in range and leaves a refused remainder in the buffer.
- A resource is the item **plus its components**: a named or enchanted stack never merges with a plain one, and a pull never replaces the buffer's components with a namesake's.
- The tick rate (`max(2, 20 − 2 × speed)`), items per operation (`1 << min(6, stacks)`), phase-spread across routers by position, and the module/filter settings in the block entity.

**Not yet ported**

- **The other modules:** Puller Mk2, Sender Mk2/3, vacuum, dropper, flinger, placer, breaker, extruder 1/2, detector, distributor, energy distributor/output, fluid 1/2, player, activator, void and creative, with their settings screens.
- **Upgrades and augments:** the 10 upgrade items and their insert rules, the 11 augments and the 5 smart filters (this slice's filter is a whitelist/blacklist over item ids).
- **The GUI** (module/upgrade/buffer slots, redstone and eco modes) and the recipe/advancement chain for the carried items.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/modularrouters/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the carried recipes and the content/loot proof: the mod's whole crafting progression — blank module, router, puller and sender — plus the router's own drop. Both were dead in 26.3, and neither error was upstream's: the carried JSON was still in the 1.21.1 dialect. The recipes used the `{"item": …}` / `{"tag": …}` ingredient form, which 26.3 rejects, so the game logged `invalid ingredient` and every recipe returned nothing; the loot table used `"conditions": [ … ]`, while 26.3 wants a singular `"condition"`, so a broken router dropped nothing. Both are converted, and the port gains two fail-capable nets: `tools/data_shape.py` checks the dialect on the built package, and `tools/craft_check.py` crafts each recipe in a real table. Proven in game: the four recipes craft with their declared counts and consume their ingredients, two wrong-ingredient controls return nothing, the router drops itself, and the log has zero `invalid ingredient` lines.
First release

projects.name: Montarc
projects.summary: Bright, colorful shader pack: soft shadows, colored light, living water, wind, and own look for the Nether and the End.
projects.description:
Bright, colorful shader pack for Horizon. Horizon had no shaders on the registry, so I made one. Style is close to Complementary Reimagined, but the code is mine, written from scratch in WGSL.

## What you get

- **Soft shadows.** Sun and moon cast them. Water and stained glass tint the light that goes through.
- **Sky and fog match.** Blue day, orange sunsets, dark blue night. Far terrain fades into the sky, no hard line at the horizon.
- **Colored light.** Torches are warm, soul fire is blue, redstone is red, sea lanterns are cyan, amethyst is purple.
- **Water that looks like water.** Waves, depth color, reflections, sun glitter and foam on the shore.
- **Wind.** Grass, flowers, crops and leaves move. Rain makes it stronger.
- **Nether and End look different.** Nether is hot and hazy, with heat shimmer. End is cold and purple.
- **29 options.** Everything can be tuned or turned off in game.

## Which version do I take?

- **1.7.1** is for Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer (the final shader API 0.2).
- **1.6.1** is for older builds that still serve shader API 0.1. The Nightly no longer loads it.
The launcher offers the one your game can run.

## Slow? Try this

- Shadow quality: Low
- Shadow map size: 1024 or 512
- Shadow distance: 64
- Water reflections: off
- Bloom: off
- Shadows: off. Biggest gain.

## Known problems

- Horizon's shader API is experimental and can change.
- Entities, block entities and particles are not shaded yet. There is no stage for them.
- Nether and End sky is vanilla. The sky stage only draws in the Overworld.
- Shadow bias may need tuning on some GPUs. If you see stripes on surfaces, change `Shadow bias`.

versions.changelog:
- Final shader API 0.2 (Horizon Nightly 2026-11-18 or newer). It reads the terrain's shaded_tint, fogs with [frame] fog = "pack" and uses fog_environment and fog_render. The look is the same as 1.6.1, with the clearer underwater fog.
- Needs no extra switch in the game. Shader API 0.1 is retired, so 1.6.1 no longer loads in the Nightly.
- Everything from 1.6.1: portals with coloured light, shadow size and distance options, own rain and snow, puddles, optional sunbeams, seabed light patterns.
- Screenshots added. Release v1.7.1 of the repository.

projects.summary: A Horizon port of morered.
projects.description:
A port of [More Red](https://github.com/Commoble/morered) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The **logic gate plate** family (diode, NOT, AND/OR/NAND/NOR, XOR/XNOR, multiplexer, 2-input AND/NAND, latch, pulse gate): a plate attaches to a face, rotates, reads its input sides, and emits 15 from its output face when its logic function passes.
- The pure model (`runtime.rs`) has upstream's function table, the 24-entry output-direction table, the clockwise input mapping, the latch's hold/reset rule and the pulse gate's edge/2-tick rule (18 tests).
- Content: eleven gate blocks plus the `stone_plate` recipe dependency, on an `end_rod` template with the real `facing`/`rotation`/`input_*`/`powered` state properties.
- The red-alloy wire posts and the spool (select, link, cut), the six bitwise plates and their wires.
- The gates are proved in game with `ctl`: a placed plate reads its inputs and drives a lamp, a 2-tick pulse arms and clears a latch, and a stone control stays dark.

**Not yet ported**

- Placement orientation: **resolved** — a plate placed through vanilla placement takes its attachment from the clicked face and its rotation from the clicked quadrant (`state_for_placement` plus `use_item_on` rod rotation).
- The coloured network cables, the bundled cable posts/spools, soldering and the wire spool's remaining modes are deferred.
- The carried `end_rod` template gives the plates their 2-px shape and collision, but there is **no lit/unlit tint** (the models' tint indices need a block-colour provider); the wire model is simplified to six 2-px plates.
- A comparator's strength collapses to a boolean (the gates are binary), and inputs are sampled once per tick: a rise and fall of one input inside a single tick collapses to no edge.
- Loot drops one wire rather than the subwire count (the pin has no equivalent of `WireCountLootFunction`).

MIT: the original copyright and licence travel inside the bundle, not only in the source repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

projects.description:
A port of [Mystical Agradditions](https://github.com/BlakeBr0/MysticalAgradditions) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The six tier-6 crops `mysticalagradditions:<name>_crop` (`nether_star`, `dragon_egg`, `gaia_spirit`, `awakened_draconium`, `neutronium`, `nitro_crystal`) on the `minecraft:wheat` template: `age` 0..7, the jar's 4-pixel outline with an empty collision, and vanilla crop random tick.
- Their seeds (`<name>_seeds`, a plain item with `place_block`, as the parent port does) and essences (`<name>_essence`).
- The six cruxes `<name>_crux` on the `minecraft:stone` template: hardness 5.0, blast resistance 10.0, `requires_tool`, and the jar's `mineable/pickaxe` + `needs_stone_tool` membership.
- `insanium_farmland` on the `minecraft:farmland` template, in `#minecraft:supports_crops`, `#minecraft:grows_crops` and `#minecraft:mineable/shovel`.
- The growth gate: a crop only grows while its own crux is two blocks below it. The parent's `requiresEffectiveFarmland` default is false; when true the block below must be insanium farmland.
- Bone meal only targets a crop that can grow and is under age 7, and never advances it (the jar's `isValidBonemealTarget`/`isBonemealSuccess`).
- 26.3 loot tables: a ripe crop gives 1 essence + 1 seed, a young one 1 seed (tier 6's `secondarySeedDrop` is false, so there is no second roll); the farmland gives itself with silk touch, else dirt + a 25% insanium essence.
- The jar's `MEM/ESE/MEM` seed recipe for `nether_star` and `dragon_egg`, the nether-star and dragon-egg crux recipes, and insanium farmland (essence + farmland), with `#c:storage_blocks/diamond` supplied as a tag.
- One tier-6 line is proved end to end in game (awakened draconium): planted, held at `random_tick_speed 0`, grown to age 7, and a survival break drops exactly 1 essence + 1 seed.

**Not yet ported**

- **Fertilized essence** is not carried (`runtime.rs` explicitly leaves it out), so no crop can be fertilized by it.
- **Four integration recipe families are missing**: the seed/crux recipes that depend on other mods' materials (`tools/carry_content.py` records which ones were dropped), so those tiers cannot be reached from survival yet.
- The remaining tiers' crops are content only where the jar defines them; the awakened-draconium line is the one proved in game.
- **This is an add-on**: it requires the parent mod **Mystical Agriculture**, whose Horizon port (`mysticalagriculture`) supplies the essence, farmland and growth rules this port builds on.

versions.changelog: Slice 3, the Wither drop: the mod's last remaining server-event behaviour, and the acquisition path for two carried recipes that were dead in survival. A Wither now leaves a withering soul at the jar's own 0.35 chance (strict `<`, tested at 0.3499 against 0.35), and `mob_drops` off adds nothing. Two measured facts are recorded rather than worked around: this pin's gamerule is `mob_drops`, not `do_mob_loot`, and `living_drops` does fire for `/kill` deaths with the dying mob resolving through the host — thirty withers left nine souls. The Ender Dragon half is `blocked(living_drops-ender-dragon)`: a probe that pushed eight scales from the hook's first line, with no host read, left nothing for a dragon killed four blocks away over 400 ticks, so the dragon's death never reaches this hook; `mob_killed` is melee-only and cannot add to a drop list, and `entity_leave_level` also fires on chunk unload. The e2e asserts that gap, so it will fail the day the pin gains the hook. Proven in game: 30 kills leave 9 souls, a zombie leaves neither drop, and the gamerule gate works.
First release: six tier-6 crops, their cruxes, insanium farmland and the awakened-draconium line, embedded in one .hnmod

The table is converted to 26.3's singular `condition` with `match_block`, matching vanilla's own `wheat.json`. But running the published 0.2.0 package's own bytes at this pin shows the old array form **still rolled correctly** — age 7 gave 1 essence and 1 seed, age 0 gave 0 essence and 1 seed — so this is dialect parity, not a behaviour repair, and `notes.md` records the measurement instead of the claim it was briefed with. projects.description:
A port of [Nature's Aura](https://github.com/Ellpeck/NaturesAura) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

- The chunk aura: drain spots (base 1,000,000 + spots) and the aura bloom (150,000 aura once, when it appears).
- The Nature's Altar's 9×4×9 multiblock and its **500,000-aura container** (300 aura a tick from the area, only in the Overworld and the Nether).

**Not yet ported**

| Gap | Shape | What the slice does instead |
|---|---|---|
| `IAuraType` per dimension | the pin has no aura-type registry | the altar pulls in the Overworld and the Nether and not in the End — upstream's rule, no type objects |
| Aura spot storage | NeoForge attaches to `LevelChunk`; the pin has `Holder::Chunk` attachments | a `ChunkAura` codec compound `{spots: [...]}`; same arithmetic |
| The client aura overlay | no client HUD in the slice | `sync: false`; the readouts are commands, and a later slice adds the overlay |
| The altar's waterlogging | the slice's templates have no waterlogged state | not carried |
| The bloom's ground set | `minecraft:poppy` allows mycelium, moss, mud and rooted dirt too | upstream's five grounds plus four extra template grounds |
| Aura-container items | the altar's "fill the held item's aura" branch | not in the slice; the tick goes straight to the recipe |

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two carried crafting recipes — and the 1.21.1 dialect they shipped in. `gold_brick` is a shapeless recipe, and the port's carry script upgraded a shaped recipe's `key` for both tag and item forms but left a shapeless `ingredients` list in the old `{"item": …}` form, so 26.3 rejected it at load and the recipe returned nothing. The script now upgrades both shapes through one helper, and regenerating the carry from the kept jar changes exactly one file of fifty-two. The port also gains the checks that would have caught it: a dialect check over the built package, a real-table craft check for both recipes with two wrong-ingredient controls, item and block read-backs, and the four carried loot tables proved by breaking them. A port of [Neo Vitae](https://github.com/breakinblocks/NeoVitae) for Horizon.

**Implemented so far**

projects.description:
A port of [Occultism](https://github.com/klikli-dev/occultism) (MIT, by klikli-dev) for Horizon. This first slice is **spirit fire**: the block, its ignition, and the chalk colours it takes.

**Implemented so far**

- `occultism:spirit_fire` on the `minecraft:torch` template (vanilla's only fire-like class with no fire damage and a sturdy-face survival rule): no collision, instant break, light 12, wool sound, purple map colour, empty drops, and a declinable `color` state with the jar's 18 values (default `white`), with the jar's animated model and blockstate.
- Ignition: flint and steel or a fire charge struck on a block with a `#occultism:start_spiritfire` item entity (datura) inside upstream's `AABB(-1,-1,-1,1,1,1)` around the clicked block's centre lights one spirit fire on the target and consumes **every** datura in that box, as upstream does. With no datura in range nothing happens and the lighter's own use runs.
- Chalk: right-clicking a spirit fire with any of the jar's chalks (16 colours, pure and impure) sets the block's `color` property.
- The datura item, the 33 chalk items, the spirit fire's own recipe, loot and language, carried inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/occultism` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

| Declared upstream library | What it would have provided | What this slice does |
|---|---|---|
| Modonomicon (required) | the guide book and its 260 pages, ritual and recipe pages | nothing: there is no guide-book reader at this pin |
| Curios (required) | accessory slots (familiar ring, spirit lamp) | nothing: there is no accessory-slot API |
| GeckoLib | the 21 animated spirit models | nothing: no spirits in this slice |
| SmartBrainLib | the spirits' job AI | nothing: no spirits in this slice |

- The remaining machines (crusher, smelter, sacrificial bowl, pentacles and rituals), every spirit and their jobs, the storage system and the dimensional mineshaft are later slices.
- The ritual and chalk recipes beyond the ones carried, and the sapling models the carried sapling item references.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices (klikli-dev, 2020) ship inside the package: `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` at its root, with the same texts in the source repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 6, the bricks tier of the building family: twelve blocks made from the two stones the package already carries, with ten crafting recipes, two smelting recipes, twelve loot tables, their models, states, textures, tags and lang. This makes twenty-two more of the family's recipes pay off. The reference's shapes are kept exactly where they differ from the obvious guess: bricks are a two-by-two into four rather than a row, and the chiseled block is made from two brick slabs rather than from bricks, so the game leg runs a four-step chain in one opened table from twelve stones down to one chiseled block, with the intermediate outputs feeding the next recipe. The cracked pair has no crafting recipe at all, it is smelting, which the leg proves in a real furnace beside a furnace with no fuel that stays idle. Every one of the twelve blocks is placed, its default state read back, and broken both by hand for nothing and with a wooden pickaxe for one. A second instance of the same reference defect is fixed rather than copied: the otherrock brick slab has no loot table in the jar while every sibling slab has one, so it would drop nothing, and this package ships the table and proves one drops. One test of my own was wrong and is recorded as such: I counted three slabs in the chiseled recipe and the reference stacks two.

Slice 5, the first tier of the otherstone and otherrock building family: slabs, stairs and walls for both stones, six blocks with their recipes, loot tables and tags, which makes thirty-eight recipes' worth of ingredients already carried finally pay off. Proven in game with the full default state of each block read back rather than a bare id: six slabs, four stairs and six walls per stone with every ingredient consumed, three dirt making nothing, both a hand break and a wooden pickaxe break asserted because these blocks do need the tool, a double slab dropping two through the table's own branch, and the wall pair joining through the wall tag. One defect in the reference is fixed rather than copied: the otherstone rock slab has no loot table in the jar at all while every sibling table ships, so upstream it drops nothing, and this port ships the table and proves one drops with a wooden pickaxe. One assertion of my own was also wrong and is recorded as such: I required a modifier list in every table and the engine does not, so the test was corrected rather than the data.

Slice 4, the crafting recipes that make an item obtainable for the first time: the dream essence, from datura fruit or from its seeds, now that the crop and its tags exist. Only two of the nineteen recipes whose result the package carries actually qualify, and the table of what was left out is part of the report: the impure chalks need a dust the package does not carry, and the otherstone building family has every ingredient but an unregistered result, so carrying its thirty-eight recipes would ship dead data. Proven in game in a real crafting table: the three-by-three fruit grid makes exactly one essence with the ingredients consumed, the same for seeds, and a mixed five-and-four grid also makes exactly one; nine dirt makes nothing, and the shapeless binding book crafts. This version also fixes a defect of our own, found only in the game: the crop harvest ran once per hand, so one click gave two fruit and six seeds, where the engine reaches the off hand only after the main hand fails. Only the main hand harvests now, and the run reads one fruit and three seeds. Two harness facts are recorded with it: a menu phase needs the offscreen renderer, and a death screen makes every later break answer that the screen is open, which silently cost two runs.

Slice 2, the datura crop and its seed source: before this the seed was creative-only, so the mod's own first step, the spirit fire loop, was unreachable in survival. A wheat-shaped crop that grows through eight ages, harvests ripe into one datura and three seeds while a young one gives a single seed, and replants itself at age zero; plus the jar's two seed modifiers on short and tall grass, two percent by hand and inverted on shears. Proven in game across four legs: the eight ages read back, a planted crop advanced from age zero to age seven under random ticks, a ripe crop dropped one fruit and three seeds while a young one dropped only a seed, and twenty-five hand breaks landed three seeds where twenty-five shear breaks dropped grass and no seed at all, which is the deterministic half of the rule. An honest gap is recorded rather than papered over: an explosion reaches the loot callback with no block at this pin, so the two percent modifier fires only on a player or mob break, and the statistical positive is reported rather than asserted because the harness cannot land hundreds of aimed breaks reliably here.

First publication, with the review repairs. Spirit fire, its datura ignition rule and the 18 chalk colours, with the jar's models, recipes and loot. `/occultism info` is now a level-2 command **with** a body re-check, and a position holding no spirit fire answers only that it is not one — the readout no longer doubles as a world probe. A spectator's click changes nothing: the hook checks the player's game mode before recolouring, lighting a fire or consuming datura, and fails closed on an unknown mode. The conversion ring is bounded and keyed per world and dimension.

projects.name: Occultism
projects.summary: Occultism by KliKli, ported to Horizon: ritual circles, spirits and their jobs, possessed creatures, the guide book, dimensional storage and the mineshaft.
projects.description:
An unofficial, alpha port to Horizon of [Occultism](https://github.com/klikli-dev/occultism), the mod by KliKli ([klikli-dev](https://github.com/klikli-dev)), made with their permission. It isn't made or supported by KliKli, so please report problems [to this port](https://github.com/Dawnforger/occultism-horizon/issues), not to them. Occultism's code is MIT and some of its art is CC BY 3.0, both credited in the package's NOTICE.

**What's in this alpha**

- **Ritual circles.** All sixteen chalks, crafted as in Occultism, with glyphs that wear down as you use them, sacrificial bowls and a golden bowl, and Occultism's rituals and pentacles, with their sacrifices and item uses.
- **The Dictionary of Spirits.** Occultism's guide book, with its ritual pages, pentacle previews placed in the world, and the ritual satchels that build a previewed circle for you.
- **Spirit names.** Books of binding carry their spirit's name, and what is made from them passes it on.
- **Working foliots.** Summoned with a job and bound to a book of calling: the janitor gathers dropped items, the transporter moves stacks between containers, the lumberjack fells and replants trees, and the farmer harvests and replants crops, each bringing what it gathers to a container.
- **Soul gems.** Capture a creature whole and let it out elsewhere.
- **Crusher, smelter and crystallizer spirits** in all four ranks, as Occultism's, at their rank's speed.
- **Possessed creatures.** Occultism's sixteen possession rituals and the creatures they make.
- **Unbound spirits.** Summon a hostile Afrit or Marid, drawn from Occultism's own models and animations, with its stats, immunities and helpers.
- **Spirit fire and Demon's Dream.** Datura, otherstone, books of binding, inks, pastes, cursed honey and more.
- **The otherworld tree.** An oak sapling in spirit fire grows into it, with its logs and fruit.
- **The Third Eye and otherworld goggles.** Raw iesnium in silver ore, otherworld logs among the oaks you chop.
- **Dimensional storage.** The Storage Actuator in Occultism's terminal look with its crafting grid, stabilizer plates, stable wormholes, the Storage Accessor, and hoppers that pull from it.
- **The dimensional mineshaft.** Miner spirits dig ores into it.

**Different from Occultism for now:** the book of calling has no screen (its mode and work area change when you use it, and its tooltip shows them); spirits take no item filters; the transporter doesn't open doors.

**Not in yet:** wild hordes, familiars, and the higher spirits' other jobs.

This is a native mod: the launcher builds it after asking you to trust its code, and it runs with your account's permissions. It contains no Minecraft code or assets. Pinned to game 26.3, Horizon SDK `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`, and fits the Nightly of 2026-11-21 (`8f83e5c`); the full corresponding source is the linked repository.

versions.changelog: Registered under its own id, occultism_horizon, because occultism is taken: id, namespaces = ["occultism"] (files, in-game ids and saved worlds are unchanged) and [incompatible] with occultism; remove any installed occultism first. Security fixes from the registry review: store ids read from items and worlds are accepted only in the mod's own form, so a forged one can't make a save write outside the world, and a soul gem's work area only at its real sizes, so a forged one can't stall the server.

0.10 and 0.11 in one step. Added: Occultism's chalk crafting in all sixteen colours, crusher spirits (in place of the Demonic Altar and its cores, removed), smelter and crystallizer spirits, sixteen possessed creatures, pastes, cursed honey and demonic meat, the otherworld tree, the spirit campfire, and the Dictionary of Spirits with pentacle previews and ritual satchels. Fixed: whole cubes on the dimensional matrix, no see-through floor under the mineshaft, Actuator and wormhole, and ritual pages' text. Security: a ritual satchel builds only for a player who may build, within reach of the place clicked, as part of the previewed pentacle and inside the world border, with at most 4 builds waiting per player; and 0.9.0-alpha.4's fixes. Same id, namespace and saved worlds as 0.9.0-alpha.4.
