projects.name: oritech
projects.summary: A Horizon port of oritech.
projects.description:
A port of [Oritech](https://github.com/Rearth/Oritech) by Rearth for Horizon — slice 1, the **Basic Generator and the Pulverizer**.

**Implemented so far**

- The Basic Generator: a 50,000 FE buffer (insert 0, extract 256 FE/call through the block energy capability), 32 FE per burning tick, fuel from the engine's `minecraft:cooking_fuel` so modded fuels work, the jar's buffer-full rule (at 49,984 FE the burn pauses and keeps its progress) and output to the six neighbours at `level_tick_post`.
- The Pulverizer: a 25,000 FE buffer, 32 FE/t while working, the jar's custom recipe type read from the pin's recipe table, progress saved with the recipe id (upstream resets after a reload; this port continues) and the jar's output-room rule.
- An operation whose result does not fit its output slot (empty or partial) **waits** instead of clamping the result, so no recipe consumes its input for a partial output.
- The seven carried pulverizer recipes, the two machine textures, the loot entries, the block entities and the English names.

**Not yet ported / deviations**

- The buffer's key is the API's int `energy` rather than upstream's long `oritech.machine_energy`; every value here fits and the buffer is a real block energy capability other mods can use.
- **The rest of Oritech:** the other generators, the accelerator ring, the reactor, the GeckoLib deep-tier models, the machines beyond these two, the ore/ingot sets and the rest of the crafting chain.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/oritech/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. CC0-1.0. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the powered furnace multiblock and the seven machine cores. It is the system rather than one machine: the core block, the assembled gate, the core lookup and "a broken core disassembles" are what the foundry, refinery, atomic forge and reactor reuse, and it closes slice 1's gameplay hole — a generator can now drive a machine that turns ore into ingots. From the jar's numbers: 10,000 FE capacity, 256 insert, 32 FE/tick, a 0.5 speed multiplier so a 200-tick recipe finishes in 100, the core at (0,1,0), seven cores with quality equal to tier, an unassembled machine inert, and a broken core freezing progress rather than losing it. The seven carried pulverizer recipes were dead data — they used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` form 26.3 rejects — and are rewritten to bare ids by the carry script. Proven in game: no core and ore with 5,000 FE smelts nothing; a core placed by right click assembles at quality 2; 320 FE finishes exactly 10 ticks and an iron ore yields one ingot for exactly 3,200 FE; a core broken mid-smelt freezes progress at 31 with the buffer unspent and a core 4 re-assembles to finish; all seven cores place and read back while machine_core_8 is refused; and all seven pulverizer recipes craft with their inputs consumed.
First release

projects.name: Petalveil
projects.summary: Vanilla's light kept whole: shadows only shade the sky's, so caves, torches and night stay vanilla. Pastel sky, waves, caustics, wind in the leaves, glow.
projects.description:
Petalveil is a shader pack in Horizon's own format, and its rule is that vanilla's light stays whole: a surface is lit by `albedo * tint * lightmap` first, and the pack only adds to it. The sun and the moon add light, and the shadow map takes back a bounded share of what comes from the sky, so a cave, a cellar, torchlight and the night keep the brightness and the colours vanilla gives them.

What it adds:
- Sun and moon shadows, soft to very soft, 1024 to 4096 texels over 64 to 160 blocks.
- A pastel sky veil that fades into vanilla's fog colour at the horizon, a rainbow while the rain dries, and a cooler night with its brightness kept.
- Broad cloud shadows drifting over the land, on their own pattern.
- Water of its own: a swell and a fine chop on the surface, rain rings, the world mirrored by fresnel, its own refraction so the bed bends with the wave, sun glitter, and caustics on the blocks under the water.
- Leaves, grass and flowers waving in a gust, the same in the shadow pass so their shadows move with them.
- Sun rays and moon rays, a soft glow, cloud edge softening, and a gentle colour grade.

Every effect can be turned off or brought to a neutral value: 59 options on five pages (Lighting, Water, Nature, Sky, Camera) in Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. Shadows off is the cheapest setting; the water's own surface detail has a switch for each part.

The pack costs about 3.8 ms of GPU time at 2560x1440 with the default settings (budget 3.0 ms). No Minecraft assets, original code.

Source: https://github.com/Givemegitpls/Petalveil — built for shader API 0.2, so it needs a Horizon Nightly from 2026-11-16 or newer.

versions.changelog:
Ported to shader API 0.2. The look is the same as 1.29.0: every stage converts at its doors (the engine's own `horizon_encode`/`horizon_decode` powers), so the values the pack's maths was tuned at are untouched, and the options keep their meaning and their defaults.

- Needs a Horizon Nightly from 2026-11-16 or newer (it reads `MaterialInput.shaded_tint`, which arrived that day).
- Nothing moved on the options pages; all 59 options keep their ids, so saved settings carry over.
- Full-bright blocks follow the new `emission`: the block's light level over 15 rather than a brightness class, so lamps in the dark are a touch dimmer than in 1.x.
- No change to the pack's cost on the GPU.

projects.name: pneumaticcraft
projects.summary: A Horizon port of pneumaticcraft.
projects.description:
A port of [PneumaticCraft: Repressurized](https://github.com/TeamPneumatic/pnc-repressurized) (GPL-3.0-only, by desht, MineMaarten and the PNC:R contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Flux Compressor**, the machine that turns FE into compressed air.

**Implemented so far**

- `pneumaticcraft:flux_compressor` with a **100,000 FE buffer**. It spends FE a tick to make **16 mL of air a tick** at 100 % heat efficiency (`40 × eff/100 × fluxCompressorEfficiency/100`, the config default 40 air per 100 FE).
- A 10,000 mL air handler with `PressureTier.TIER_TWO` (danger 20 bar, critical 25 bar), and the heat exchanger: capacity 100, `addHeat(air/20)` a tick, ambient 300 K and `(T − 300)/101` lost a tick — so it settles at about 300.8 K and stays at 100 % efficiency.
- With nothing connected the compressor **leaks** `(int)(pressure × 40) + 20` mL a tick, as upstream does, so a lone compressor never accumulates air (measured: 16 mL after 118 ticks).
- Every 5 ticks the compressor refreshes its rates; `/pneumaticcraft` readout commands expose the buffer, the air and the temperature for the harness, and the carried model, texture, language and recipe ride inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The **pressure tubes** (`pressure_tube`, `advanced_pressure_tube`, `reinforced_pressure_tube`, `tube_junction`) and tube modules — the network proper: the six-sided connection state, tube volume aggregation, network leaks, modules and camouflage. This is the next slice and the block most of the mod stands on.
- The upgrades (speed, volume, security, dispenser) and their items.
- The menus and screens, the pressure gauge and manometer items, and the GUI redstone modes.
- The overpressure explosion (`doOverpressureChecks`): nothing in this slice reaches the critical pressure without the harness, and the harness clamps at 25 bar.

GPL-3.0-only, like the original; the full licence and the original copyright notices travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, pressure tubes and the network between them: the three tubes, their six-sided connection state, per-tube volumes and tiers, network dispersion by volume, and the dead-end leak. Deferred within the same gap line: the pneumatic wrench and closed sides, tube modules, camouflage, waterlogging and the junction. One trap is recorded for every future cable-like port: a block-entity write made **during** a tick is overwritten by that entity's own write-back — a four-handler network at 25 bar lost about 200,000 mL in 40 ticks that way — so the port now applies writes in `level_tick_post` as deltas on the target's current value. Proven in game: a pair moves 2,216 mL for 5,560 FE in 139 ticks; a chain at 24.90 bar feeds a dynamo from 3,648 to 9,490 FE; a ring of four splits 4,000 mL into four 1,000 mL tubes; a dead end vents to 16 mL over 221 ticks; and each tube tier keeps upstream's volume when it is alone.
First release

projects.name: pocketstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of pocketstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [Pocket Storage](https://github.com/Flanks255/PocketStorage) (MIT, by Flanks255) for Horizon. This first slice is the **tier-1 storage unit**: a pocket-sized container whose contents ride the item stack itself.

**Implemented so far**

- `pocketstorage:psu_1`, one of the four tiers the jar ships, built on the `minecraft:iron_ingot` template with `max_stack_size: 1`, with the jar's own model and texture.
- **8 slots of 255**: upstream's `PSUTier.TIER1` (`slots = 8`, `capacity = 0xFF = 255`), repeated in its `README.MD` and in the jar's language file ("Holds %s different items, up to %s of each"). Insert tops up the slot holding the same item, else takes the first empty slot, else refuses the stack.
- The contents ride the stack's own component (`pocketstorage:contents`, one compound per filled slot), so a unit that is saved, thrown or picked up keeps what it holds; an empty unit carries no component at all and stacks like a new one.
- Sneak + right-click a container **deposits** all but one of each kind into it (upstream's `giveItems` rule); sneak + left-click **withdraws** the kinds the unit already holds (upstream's `takeItems` rule). A withdraw takes only plain stacks: a damaged, renamed or enchanted container stack is refused rather than rebuilt from its id, because a saved slot is one `{id, count}` entry and flattening it would destroy the components.
- `/psu put|list|help` stands in for upstream's screen, which this slice does not carry.

**Not yet ported**

- Tiers 2 to 4 (`psu_2` 16 × 4,095, `psu_3` 32 × 65,535, `psu_4` 64 × 1,048,575): only the tier-1 item is carried. The runtime already holds all four tiers' numbers, but the items, models, tabs and the upgrade path are not shipped.
- The `pocketstorage:upgrade` recipe type: a shaped recipe whose `D` is the previous unit, needing a `ShapedRecipe.pattern` access transformer. The pin has no custom recipe type a port can register, so a tier 2–4 recipe cannot be authored yet; the three upgrade recipes are a named gap.
- The storage unit screen, its item handler and the keybind that opens it.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/pocketstorage/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, tiers 2 to 4 and the three upgrade recipes. Tiers 2, 3 and 4 are now carried — 16 by 4,095, 32 by 65,535 and 64 by 1,048,575 — and the upgrade path is authored as data, with `pocketstorage:upgrade` copying the old unit's contents onto the next tier so nothing is lost. The port's own gap note said the pin had no custom recipe type a port could register; that was stale — at this pin a mod registers a crafting kind (`CraftingRecipeKind` plus `register_crafting_recipe_serializer`) and the engine loads it into the crafting table, so the recipes are real data rather than a code special case. Proven in game: tier 1 crafts; gold around it makes a tier 2 that carries the 30 diamonds the old unit held; the same step reaches tier 3 and tier 4, whose readout is one of 64 kinds with 30 items and 1,048,575 each at most; a fourth step produces nothing; and every craft consumes its ingredients. The counterfactual flips the "the upgraded unit kept its 30 diamonds" assertion and exits 1.
First release

projects.name: Powah
projects.summary: The starter Furnator, Energy Cell and Energy Cable: generation, storage and FE transfer, ported.

versions.changelog: Slice 6, the two ladders completed: six more furnator tiers and six more cable tiers, so the furnator now runs from eighty FE a tick to forty thousand and the cable from two thousand to a million. Proven by reading every one of the fourteen numbers in game rather than by trusting the table: each furnator clamps at its own buffer under a request for far more than it can hold, each cable names its own rate in its readout, and the difference is observable through the blocks they feed, where a cell behind a starter cable takes five hundred a tick and the same cell behind a basic one takes a thousand. The nitro furnator is the one worth quoting, because its buffer was given exactly room for one coal so the read can be checked against the fuel rather than the machine: carbon reads eight thousand, not forty-seven thousand nine hundred and eighty. All eighteen new recipes craft with their exact outputs and ingredients consumed, and all twelve new blocks drop themselves. A selftest that demands the old rate fails, and the whole scenario on a game without the package fails at the first placement. Reactors stay recorded as blocked, because their fuel has no source in this pack at all.

Slice 2: the dielectric and capacitor family — six items and eight recipes — so the three carried machine recipes finally craft. The leg drives a real crafting table through all eleven: paste, rods, casing, both capacitors, the furnator, the energy cell and the cables, asserting each result's id and count and that every ingredient is consumed (the lava bucket leaving its bucket), with an off-pattern grid leaving the result empty.

projects.name: pvp_music
projects.summary: A Horizon port of PvP Music.
projects.description:
A 1:1 Rust port of [PvP Music](https://modrinth.com/mod/pvp-music) (CC0-1.0),
which plays battle music when you engage a player or (if enabled) a mob.
Upstream publishes no source repository, so the port follows the documented
behavior. The package is the .hmod source: a native mod built against the
pinned Horizon SDK (api 0.2, game 26.3).

## Behavior (the original's, kept)

- Mutual-combat detection: attacks on and by players and mobs are remembered
  for 5 s; a landed hit on a player opens the 500 ms target confirm, and a
  mob fight starts when both sides have recently attacked each other.
- The wither and explosion triggers, with their own radii.
- The fading battle track: per-tick volume, death fades when you die or the
  target dies, and the short and long end sounds queued when a battle of
  30 s or more ends.
- The phased two-half battle music, switched at low health on a beat.
- Settings through /pvpmusic (short form /pvm): volume, fades, the mob
  rules, the phase lengths, the beat, the end thresholds and the disabled
  mob list, exactly the original's config fields.

## Wiring

- music (client): the state machine runs once a tick and answers the track
  and its volume, replacing vanilla's situational music while a battle
  plays, and leaves vanilla's when idle.
- client_attack_target (client): records our attack clicks as combat
  candidates.
- client_tick_pre (client): refreshes the max-health read, detects a health
  drop as a hurt, and plays the queued end sound once the battle stopped.
- command + register_client_commands: /pvpmusic, answered locally, shown as
  a chat line, and consumed so the game does not run it.
- The battle tracks and end sounds ship as assets/pvp_music/sounds/.

## Horizon seams

Where the client cannot see what the original read, the port degrades the
same way the original's own fallbacks do: a click on a player opens the
target confirm (the API's client attack hook fires before the server
confirms the hit), and a health drop records a hurt with an unknown source
so the machine's own mob fallbacks apply. Both are the client-side combat
facts the port needs; the ask is filed on horizon-rust/horizon as issue
#10064 and tracked until patched, at which point the wiring switches to it
directly.

projects.name: rangedpumps
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rangedpumps.
projects.description:
A port of [Ranged Pumps](https://github.com/refinedmods/rangedpumps) (MIT, by Refined Mods) for Horizon. The pump drains still fluid sources in an expanding square scan and collects them in its own tank.

**Implemented so far**

- `rangedpumps:pump` with per-block range setting, the carried model, texture, language, recipe and loot, declared as one content pack inside the `.hnmod`.
- The scan: `range` starts at -1 (the single column directly **below** the pump); each later range is the **perimeter** of a `(2r+3)²` square — the 8, 16, 24… block ring at horizontal distance `r+1`. Inside a column the pump goes down one block per 8 ticks (upstream's `speed`) to the dimension's minimum Y, then starts the next column. The interior of a ring is not scanned, as upstream.
- Draining: only `minecraft:water` and `minecraft:lava` at `level=0` (a still source) are taken, one bucket at a time, into a 32-bucket internal tank; each drained source is replaced with air and then with the configured block (stone by default), so neighbouring fluid updates see the removal.
- The tank is declared as the block's fluid capability and pushed into neighbouring fluid handlers once per block tick, an equal share to each (upstream's `fillNeighbors`).
- `/rangedpumps` readout and configuration commands.

**Not yet ported**

- No energy (FE) gating: the pin has the energy API, but this slice has no FE source, so the pump runs as if `useEnergy = false`.
- No redstone pause: reading a neighbour's signal needs `LevelAccess`/`Ticks` at this pin.
- The pump's screen and its upgrade items; only the command path sets the range.

The scan no longer consumes a position it could not drain: a source the tank cannot take stays in the world and is retried on the next tick, and a column that starts below the dimension's floor (a pump on the bottom block) is skipped instead of descending forever. MIT; the original copyright and permission notices (Refined Mods) travel inside the archive at `mixins/rangedpumps/LICENSE`.

projects.name: refinedstorage
projects.summary: A Horizon port of refinedstorage.
projects.description:
A port of [Refined Storage 2](https://github.com/refinedmods/refinedstorage2) by Refined Mods for Horizon — slice 1, the item network.

**Implemented so far**

- **Network:** the connected component of the four network blocks over face-adjacent positions, capped at 512 blocks. A component with a controller is **online**; without one nothing works (upstream: the controller is the network's root and every node is inactive without it). The grid's `active` block state and the `/refinedstorage info` line both read it.
- **Cable connections** (upstream `computeConnections`): six boolean state properties (`north/east/south/west/up/down`), each written from whether the neighbour is a network block.
- **Disk Drive** with nine disk slots, and the **1k Storage Disk** whose items live in its item component, so the disk carries its contents when moved.
- **Grid:** a 9×6 menu that searches the network, withdraws and deposits. Two grids never show the same items — each grid's view sets aside what the other open grids already show — so the last ten diamonds cannot be taken twice.
- A deposit the network refuses stays in the slot **as its remainder only**, so a full disk cannot duplicate the items the player tried to add.
- The `/refinedstorage info|filter` commands, the four blocks' content (models, textures, loot, tags, creative tab) and the disk's component.

**Not yet ported**

- **No energy:** the controller is the network's on/off root but consumes and stores nothing; its `energy_type` state has two values where upstream has four.
- **The rest of the mod:** crafters, exporters/importers, external storage, interfaces, relays, network transmitters/receivers, the security manager, the wireless transmitter/grid, the portable grid, the crafting/pattern grids, autocrafting, fluid storage and disks, the other disk sizes (4k/16k/64k/creative), storage blocks, upgrades, the config file and the coloured variants of every block.
- **No recipes:** the five items need Refined Storage's own chain (`quartz_enriched_iron`, `machine_casing`, processors, cores, `1k_storage_part`, `storage_housing`) and NeoForge `#c:` tags, so they come from the creative tab.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/refinedstorage/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`, with Refined Mods' MIT notice) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: Slice 6, the upgrade items: the transmitter's four upgrade slots and the range upgrade that makes the sixteen-block rule a starting point rather than a ceiling. Only the range half is real here and the other eight upgrades are refused rather than shipped, because speed, stack, regulator and autocrafting bind to importers, exporters, destructors and the crafting grid, none of which this port has, and the four enchantment upgrades need a recipe type the pin does not offer. The numbers are read from the reference rather than guessed: eight blocks per upgrade, four slots, and the creative variant at the top of the priority chain. Proven in game with the differential the brief asked for: a use at seventeen blocks is refused at sixteen and accepted at twenty-four once one range upgrade sits in a slot, the creative upgrade takes the same transmitter to unlimited, the transmitter's own menu shows four slots, and a diamond shift-clicked into that menu does not enter an upgrade slot. The dimension rule is unaffected and still refuses a use from another dimension with an unlimited range in place. This version also fixes a port defect: the transmitter's template could never open a menu, because the game posts the open only for a container class, so the block keeps its nub shape and collision through declared shapes while carrying a container template, and the binding moved to the block's own click hook because the container's click runs first.

projects.name: Refined Types
projects.summary: An add-on for Refined Storage that stores FE, Source and Souls: storage blocks, disks and a Network Energizer.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [Refined Types](https://github.com/starforcraft/Refined-Types) by **Starforcraft** (MIT) — an add-on for Refined Storage that stores what Refined Storage does not: FE, Source and Souls. Storage blocks add their tier's capacity to the network, storage disks carry their amount in
the item and live in the network's disk drives, and the Network Energizer keeps the network supplied
from the energy storage. Scoped to that storage: the typed grid, exporters, importers, external
storage, autocrafting, the storage screens and the recipes are the port's gap list, not this
version.

**Implemented so far:** the slice in the package, as described above.

**Not yet ported**

- The typed grid, exporters, importers, external storage, autocrafting and storage-monitor insertion — that half needs Refined Storage's Java API and is the recorded gap, not this slice.
- **Recipes are not carried.** Every one needs `refinedstorage:machine_casing` (the parent has no crafting chain), `c:dusts/redstone` (a NeoForge tag absent at 26.3) and `neoforge:conditions` (no such loader condition at 26.3); the 111 recipes and their advancement unlocks would be dead data, so the items come from the creative menu until the parent's chain exists.
- The storage-block and energizer screens, block contents surviving a break, and `fireResistant` as upstream declares it.
- The energizer does not refill its buffer from the network once drained — upstream does not either: the buffer is a load-time kick-start. The network is not shut down when unpowered (the parent has no such state); storage stays readable and `active` says whether the usage was covered.
- Source and Soul have no consumer at this pin (no exporters, and Ars Nouveau / the soul mod are not ported), so their role is capacity, totals and usage.
- A storage block beside a cable does not appear in the parent's cable connection state.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the recipe family: 107 of the jar's 109 recipes carried and converted to the 26.3 dialect — 27 blocks, 27 shaped disks, 27 shapeless housing-based disks and 26 parts — now that the parent mod ships the machine casing, the processors, the storage housing, the 1k part and the common tags they need. The two left out are left out with their reason printed rather than faked: the network energizer needs a parent block this campaign has not ported, and the 64b source storage part needs a namespace that is not in the registry. Proven in game: every one of the 107 crafts with its declared output and count and consumes its ingredients, and 107 deliberate wrong-ingredient controls leave the result empty, so the recipe list is not passing on a loose match. The jar's own 109 files were in the 1.21.1 object form the 26.3 loader rejects, which is what made them dead data in the first place.

projects.name: repeatable_trial_vaults
projects.summary: A Horizon port of repeatable_trial_vaults.
projects.description:
A port of [Repeatable Trial Vaults](https://github.com/Buuz135/Repeatable-Trial-Vaults) by Buuz135 for Horizon — the key-reset slice.

**Implemented so far**

- Right-clicking a `minecraft:vault` with `minecraft:trial_key` or `minecraft:ominous_trial_key` resets it **iff** the acting player's UUID is in `rewarded_players`: the click is cancelled (the block never sees it), the held stack loses the vault config's key count (normally 1; a keyless vault consumes 0; creative is skipped as `ItemStack.consume` does), the `used` stat is awarded once and the hand swings.
- The reset is allowed whatever the vault's `vault_state` is (upstream checks no state). The vault's own tick then sees the player as unrewarded and rolls loot again, so a vault is repeatable without a restart.
- The trial-key item tags and the English names in a valid content archive.

**Not yet ported**

- Reading and writing a **vanilla** block entity has no native API here: the port reaches the game's own block-entity map and the vault's `rewarded_players` directly, a pin-internal dependency recorded as an issue-shaped gap (a native read/write hook for a vanilla block entity's saved NBT).
- The item tag cannot be read where the port runs (`native_item_in_tag` returns `NotServer` on a client execution), so the key check reads the item id.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/repeatable_trial_vaults/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

The upstream 1.0.3 tag ships a CC0-1.0 LICENSE file while the same tag's NeoForge metadata declares MIT; this port takes the material under MIT, with CC0-1.0 available as the alternative.

projects.name: restrictions
projects.summary: A Horizon port of restrictions.
projects.description:
A port of [Restrictions](https://github.com/McJtyMods/Restrictions) (MIT, by McJty) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Attractor** and the **Pusher**: blocks that pull or push the mobs in front of them.

**Implemented so far**

- Attractor and Pusher: the cells in front of the block, `pos + facing*1 … pos + facing*signal` (the block's own cell excluded), where `signal` is the strongest neighbouring redstone signal (0 means off). Each server tick, every mob whose **bounding box intersects** one of those cells gets a velocity impulse along the facing: **−0.1** blocks/tick for the attractor (toward the block) and **+0.1** for the pusher (away). A cell is tested by intersection when the entity has a bounding box, with the feet-cell test as the fallback for entity kinds that have none — so a tall mob is drawn in even when its feet are a cell lower. No line-of-sight test (upstream has none).
- The block entity is created by the `block_entity` hook and ticks through `block_entity_ticks`; the facing is read from the block's `facing` property, and the redstone signal from the neighbouring cells each tick.
- The carried models, textures, language, recipes and loot, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.
- `/restrictions` readout commands for the harness.

**Not yet ported**

- One Way and One Way Wall: upstream's One Way is `noCollission()` and applies its push on `entityInside`. Horizon's content format couples outline and collision and has no per-entity collision shape, and there is no neutral no-collision template with a block entity — deferred to an engine API.
- Players and item entities cannot be moved at this pin (there is no player velocity or position write, and item entities have no position setter), so the blocks move **mobs only**.
- Arrows, boats and orbs are out of scope, as is McJtyLib's two-block placement of the taller variants.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/restrictions/LICENSE`.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the sweep is every entity rather than only mobs. Upstream pulls everything the host can move — dropped items, arrows, boats, minecarts, experience orbs — and the port's filter was a leftover from the retired hook that moved only mobs. The exclusion is now a player, whose client owns its motion, and the per-cell budget covers every kind. Proven in game with a differential on the same lane: a powered attractor pulls a dropped item from 3.5 blocks to 1.125 and an experience orb from 5.5 to 1.25, while both unpowered controls stay at their starting distance to four decimals. This version also fixes a defect in the port's own shipped data: both mover loot tables named a component from a library this package does not carry, so a real pickaxe break copied nothing and the block dropped nothing at all — the modifier is gone and a break now drops one block with a pickaxe and one by hand, with vanilla stone as the differential. One pin limitation is recorded rather than papered over: the needs-stone-tool tag has no tier gate at this pin, so a wooden pickaxe still drops the block. Every carried recipe is now crafted from the delivered package's own JSON, with ingredients consumed and the grid left empty.
First release

projects.name: rftoolsbase
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rftoolsbase.
projects.description:
A port of [RFTools Base](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsBase) by McJty for Horizon — slice 1, the Machine Infuser.

**Implemented so far**

- `rftoolsbase:machine_infuser` on the stonecutter template with a horizontal `facing`, standard-iron properties and the jar's own model and front texture, placed facing the player.
- A 60,000 FE buffer through the block energy capability: any side may fill it 600 FE a call, nothing may drain it (upstream's `GenericEnergyStorage(…, canExtract = false)`).
- Two slots: slot 0 takes `rftoolsbase:shards`, slot 1 takes one infusable machine and is also the output; every face reaches both and automation may take from slot 1.
- The infusion rule from the jar: with a shard and an infusable machine below 256 it spends `(int)(600 × (2 − level/256) / 2)` FE plus one shard and infuses for 5 ticks, raising the machine one level. The cost comes from the block's own level, not the item's.
- The `rftoolsbase:infused` item component (0..=256), seeded from the placed item, with the `Infused: N%` tooltip, and a two-slot menu with four data slots (energy, capacity, `infusing`, block level).
- The carried blockstate, models, texture, recipes, loot, tags, creative tab and English names.

**Not yet ported**

- The tablet, the crafter, the storage scanner and the other RFTools machines (those live in RFTools Storage/Utility/Control, separate mods).
- The block-protector/security chain, the config file and the in-game documentation items.
- Recipes that need items from the unported RFTools mods.

The original copyright and licence notices travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/rftoolsbase/LICENSE` and `NOTICE.md`) and are also in this repository. MIT. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

versions.changelog: A repin rather than a new family, and it buys something no single port could: the RFTools family can now be built into one game. This port was pinned to an older build of the engine, and a game refuses two packages that disagree, so a sibling port could not craft its own recipe in the same world as this one. Moved to the campaign pin, rebuilt twice byte-identically, and the whole ladder re-run. The proof is the thing it unblocks: a three-package game carrying this port, the storage port and the power port, in which the storage scanner is crafted from a real machine frame in a real crafting table with the frame consumed, a stone in the frame's cell crafts nothing, and the coal generator is likewise crafted from its own frame, with the result taken out of the slot and the inventory asserted for every ingredient. A run against the unmodified game fails at the first give, as it must, and an inverted assertion fails too. Two harness facts came out of it: a give lands on the next tick, and the launcher reuses a build when the manifest is unchanged, so the version bump is what forces the recompile.
First release

projects.name: RFTools Builder
projects.summary: RFTools Builder for Horizon: the Builder block and its shape cards. A card carries a shape (box, sphere, cylinder, capped cylinder, prism, cone, top and…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of RFTools Builder 1.21-7.0.8: the Builder block and its shape cards, plus the shape geometry behind them. A card carries a shape, a size, an offset and whether it is solid or hollow, and the Builder walks that shape placing blocks into it from a container above or below. Upstream: https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsBuilder — licence **MIT**.

**Implemented so far**

- The shape card `rftoolsbuilder:shape_card_def` carries shape, size, offset, solidity and the corner-selection state in its `rftoolsbuilder:shape_card` component, and a stack with no component is the jar's default solid 5×5×5 box.
- The jar's ten shape formulas — box, sphere, top and bottom dome, cylinder, capped cylinder, prism, torus, heart and cone — are transcribed cell for cell, with the float arithmetic, the integer truncation and the per-axis centre nudge.
- Solid and hollow follow upstream's border test, where a cell is in the shell when one of its six neighbours is outside, and the jar's quirks are kept (a hollow cylinder has no cap, only its rim).
- Dimension is clamped into 0–512 and offset into −260–260, and a card whose box exceeds 50,000,000 cells is refused with those numbers.
- Cards are authored by sneak-right-clicking a Builder and clicking two corners, and by `/rftoolsbuilder shape|offset|reset` for shapes corners cannot express.
- The Builder block entity walks the shape from the top down with x fastest at eight cells a tick, takes the first placeable block from the container above it or below if that one is empty, and waits at a cell it has no block for.
- A protection gate skips a cell outside the world border before anything is read or taken, so a protected cell is never built and never charged a block.
- `/rftoolsbuilder status <pos>` prints shape, size, offset, cell count, progress and the first refused cell, with the count bounded and cached so a huge sparse shape cannot stall the server thread.
- The upstream walk defect is fixed: a shape straddling a chunk boundary is built completely instead of losing the cells in the earlier chunk.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control and a selftest that both fail without it.

**Not yet ported**

- The quarry is not carried, nor its resource scan, silk and fortune drops, void list, replacement block or chunk loading; upstream's quarry is a card type with no geometry, so no quarry shape was invented.
- The movers with their control pages and vehicle builder, the shields with their projector and renderer, and the space chamber with the copy, move and swap modes it feeds are not carried.
- The composer, the projector and the scanner are not carried, which is also why the composition and scan shapes are missing.
- The GUI screens and the mod's own networking are replaced here by the commands and the action bar.
- The liquid and pump cards, the filter module (which is why the container has one slot) and energy are not carried, so this slice builds without power.
- A placed block's own placement hook does not run, because the pin has no fake player, so a bed or door appears only half placed.
- Chunk loading is replaced by waiting for a loaded chunk, and the hilight mode, progress HUD and renderer are not carried.
- Spawn protection is not enforced, because the pin cannot read it, so only the world border is checked.

Ported from the upstream mod (MIT); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the two carried recipes, which were dead data: the builder and its shape card both used the 1.21.1 `{"item": …}` / `{"tag": …}` ingredient form, which 26.3 rejects at load, so the game logged `invalid ingredient` for every key and the grid sat full with an empty result — the mod could not be crafted at all. Both files now use bare item ids and `#tag` strings, with patterns, results and ids untouched, and the port gains a data guard that fails on the old shape. Proven in game: the shape card and the builder both craft with their ingredients consumed and the grid emptied, two wrong-ingredient controls return nothing, the game log has no `invalid ingredient` line, and a broken builder drops itself once.

projects.name: rftoolspower
projects.summary: A Horizon port of rftoolspower.
projects.description:
A port of [rftoolspower](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsPower) by McJtyMods. The generator and monitor recipes use RFTools Base ingredients, provided by `rftoolsbase` 0.2.2 on the matching SDK.

The first port of RFTools Power, and it opens with the coal generator: a machine whose whole loop closes inside one block — fuel in, burn, FE out, and a `lit` state that mirrors the burn. Upstream's numbers, not invented ones: 60 FE a tick, 600 ticks for a coal and 5,400 for a coal block, a 500,000 FE buffer, one insert-only slot. Proven in game across thirteen phases: a fresh generator reads 0 of 500,000 and unlit; one coal puts 780 FE in the buffer at 587 of 600 burn and empties the player's hand; the energy gain equals exactly sixty times the burn delta over fifty-three ticks; the store freezes when the burn ends; stone is refused and charcoal burns for its own 600; a hopper feeds the slot with no click at all; the full store survives a save and relaunch; and a generator broken in survival drops an item carrying its 3,000 FE, which restores on placing while a doctored 999,999 is clamped to the 500,000 ceiling. Two deviations are recorded rather than hidden: there is no GUI, so a right click fuels the machine, and the lit state is the same cube because the parent's glow overlay cannot run at this pin. The powercell family is recorded as blocked on the smart wrench, which the parent port does not carry.

versions.changelog: Slice 4, the endergenic generator and the pearl injector: the mod's signature mechanic, where a pearl is fired at a generator and pays according to how far the generator has charged. Every figure is read from the reference's own configuration rather than guessed: the charging window is modes one through fifteen with everything else idle, the payment per mode runs from two hundred FE to twenty-five thousand six hundred with the mod's factor already applied, the flight time is a third of the distance plus one tick capped at four, and the loss chance is five in a thousand. Proven in game with parsed replies: a fired pearl arrives and pays exactly two hundred while the store moves by the gained minus the spent, the same shot against an idle destination drops the pearl and pays nothing with the reason named, and with no injector the charge runs and decays without earning anything. A hundred thousand FE next to the receiver hands over ninety-eight thousand and keeps two thousand as the reserve. A broken generator carries its three thousand and restores it, the monitor facing it reads the store, and the store, the arrival and the link all survive a relaunch.

Slice 3, the powercell: the mod's core storage, a block that holds five hundred thousand FE and shares it with its neighbours as one network. Its side faces default to none, so a fresh cell takes nothing until a face is set to input, which is upstream's own behaviour and the reason this family was blocked without the wrench: the stand-in is a command that sets one face at a time. Two numbers in our brief did not survive the jar and both made the port more faithful. A lone tier-one cell accepts two hundred and fifty FE a tick, not two thousand, because the reference caps what it receives by its own per-tick figure; the leg asserts the cell's gain and the generator's matching loss. And a tier-two cell beside a tier-one one does share the network, because membership is adjacency and the reference recurses without a tier test; the differential is a tier-two cell one block further away reading its own empty store. Proven in game across the sequence that matters: a fresh cell refuses a hundred thousand FE over forty ticks, one face set to input takes exactly two hundred and fifty a tick for thirty-eight ticks with the generator losing the same, and an output face likewise. Two defects only the game found are recorded: a pure item needs its own item declaration or a give refuses it while the recipe still crafts, and setting the same block again keeps its block entity data, which made one phase vacuous until it was cleared.

Slice 2, the power monitor: a block that reads the machine behind it every twenty ticks and shows how full it is, as a level state and as redstone, so a generator's charge is finally visible from outside. The ratio is the reference's own, one plus five steps of charge, and the bands are settable the way its GUI would set them. Proven in game across three readings and two controls: a generator at half its buffer reads level three, an empty one reads level one, and plain stone reads level zero because it is not an energy block; a band of forty to sixty lights the lamp at fifty percent and a band of ninety to a hundred puts it out; and the generator's own push, which this slice also adds, empties a hundred thousand FE into an adjacent receiver in two-thousand-FE steps while the monitor facing that receiver reads full. One limit is stated rather than papered over: a monitor has no buffer of its own in the reference, so the push is proven against a receiver that exists only in the test harness, and the delivered package invents no buffer to make the assertion easier.

The first port of RFTools Power, and it opens with the coal generator: a machine whose whole loop closes inside one block — fuel in, burn, FE out, and a `lit` state that mirrors the burn. Upstream's numbers, not invented ones: 60 FE a tick, 600 ticks for a coal and 5,400 for a coal block, a 500,000 FE buffer, one insert-only slot. Proven in game across thirteen phases: a fresh generator reads 0 of 500,000 and unlit; one coal puts 780 FE in the buffer at 587 of 600 burn and empties the player's hand; the energy gain equals exactly sixty times the burn delta over fifty-three ticks; the store freezes when the burn ends; stone is refused and charcoal burns for its own 600; a hopper feeds the slot with no click at all; the full store survives a save and relaunch; and a generator broken in survival drops an item carrying its 3,000 FE, which restores on placing while a doctored 999,999 is clamped to the 500,000 ceiling. Two deviations are recorded rather than hidden: there is no GUI, so a right click fuels the machine, and the lit state is the same cube because the parent's glow overlay cannot run at this pin. The powercell family is recorded as blocked on the smart wrench, which the parent port does not carry.

projects.name: rftoolsstorage
projects.summary: Modular storage: a module block holding 6,400 items, sealed until locked.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [RFTools Storage](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsStorage) (MIT, by **McJty**) for Horizon. This first slice is **modular storage**.

**Implemented so far**

- **`rftoolsstorage:modular_storage`** holds a storage module and stores items in it: tier 1 is the jar's own **100 slots × 64 = 6,400 items**, with `StorageModuleItem.MAXSIZE = {100,200,300,500,…}` driving the tiers.
- **The block is inert until a module is installed and the storage is locked**, exactly as the jar's `insertItem`/`extractItem` both begin with `if (!isLocked())`.
- **The player surface:** a module held in hand installs into the block, a held stack inserts on right-click, an empty hand seals or withdraws, and the action bar reports `stored/capacity`; `/rftoolsstorage info|lock <x> <y> <z>` reads and seals it.
- **Contents survive a save, quit and relaunch**, one item kind per slot with the stack limit respected.

**Not yet ported**

- the storage scanner, the crafting manager, tiers 2–4, the remote module and remote block;
- the type, filter, dump and control modules and the storage tablet;
- the GUI (search, sort, compact, cycle, padlock) — this slice uses right-clicks and commands;
- the fill overlay: the jar declares its `amount`/`type` states but never writes them (upstream's `getRenderLevel()` is a commented `// @todo 1.14` stub), so the port does not invent one either.

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 5, the storage scanner: a block that reads the inventories inside a cube around it and answers one command with what it found, charging its own energy for the question and refusing when it has none. The radius is settable because the reference exposes it as a slider, so here it is a command that clamps to the same bounds. Proven in game as a sequence of exact answers: a fresh scanner with no power says so with its buffer in the reply; at the default radius it sees nothing because the chest is two blocks away and reports its charge falling; at radius two it finds sixty-four stone and no dirt; at radius three it finds the dirt too, each answer costing the same fixed charge; with the buffer emptied it refuses and reads nothing, and recharging makes it answer again. A chest and a modular storage both answer that they are not scanners, the buffer and radius and answer all survive a relaunch, and a survival break drops the block itself. Two honest restrictions are recorded rather than worked around: the scanner's recipe needs a machine frame from a sibling port that is pinned at an older build and so cannot share this game, and the claimed-land check is blocked because the pin exposes a cancellable destroy hook rather than a permission query.
First release

projects.name: rftoolsutility
projects.summary: The RFTools tank: 32,000 mB of one fluid, filled and drained with a bucket.
projects.description:
A Horizon port of [RFTools Utility](https://github.com/McJtyMods/RFToolsUtility) (MIT, by **McJty**) for Horizon. This first slice is **the tank**.

**Implemented so far**

- **`rftoolsutility:tank`, 32,000 mB of one fluid** — the jar's own manual says "up to 32 buckets" and `TankConfiguration.maxCapacity` defaults to 32,000 mB.
- **Every face accepts and provides** the fluid, and the contents live in the block entity's saved data, so they survive a save, quit and relaunch.
- **The bucket loop:** a water or lava bucket fills it by 1,000 mB and leaves an empty bucket in hand, an empty bucket drains 1,000 mB and fills, and a full tank, a different fluid or a partial amount is refused.
- **A declared level 0–8** picks the jar's own `tank0…tank8` textures, and `/rftoolsutility info|tank` reads and sets the contents.

**Not yet ported**

- the mod's other four families: the teleporters, the screens and their 30 modules, the logic gates, the environmental controller, the spawner and the three crafters;
- the tank's own GUI (this slice uses the commands);
- fluid push/pull between neighbouring tanks (the slice is the bucket and tank loop).

Original copyright and licence notices are kept in this repository. Pinned to Horizon `0b14f8a` and horizon-mixins `e59da90`. Help with the remaining slices is welcome.

versions.changelog: Slice 8, the matter beamers: a block that eats a stack of material and sends matter to a spawner it is linked to, which closes the feed half of the matter gate. The beamer reads a recipe's three material sources itself rather than trusting the recipe's older object form, and it carries the four living tags so the empty living form yields its own reduced amounts. Proven in game with parsed values across nine phases: a link to a stone block is refused, to a spawner four blocks away is made, a target twelve blocks away is refused and a beamer cannot link to itself; eight items and four thousand FE give exactly two sends, the store growing by two for the first material, two for the list form and three for the living form at its one and a half per block, with the buffer emptied; cobblestone is refused with both the items and the energy kept; no power and no redstone send nothing; and a broken beamer carries its link, its count, its energy and its contents back. Two defects in the reference are fixed rather than copied: it spends the energy before it knows the material is accepted and burns it on a refusal, and it consumes a zero-yield living item for no matter. The link is a command because no wrench exists in this port or its parent, and the twenty tick clock is the tick's own game time rather than a saved counter.

Slice 7, the spawner's matter gate: a spawn now needs three matter amounts as well as its energy, and it spends each by its own amount. Our brief called for three fluid tanks and the artefact says otherwise: the reference stores three floats in the machine's own data, filled by a beamer that sends an item rather than a fluid, and there is no fluid anywhere in that module. So the port keeps the three floats, and a command writes what a beamer's send would add, which is provenance rather than an API gap — the pin can declare fluids, it is simply not what this machine does, and inventing them would have let pipes feed a spawner that upstream cannot feed. Proven in game with a three-step differential on the same machine: eight hundred FE and empty stores spawn nothing and spend nothing; stores a hair short of the recipe spawn nothing and keep both their energy and their matter; exactly enough spawns one zombie and leaves the energy at zero with all three stores emptied. A second spawn spends each store by its own amount and leaves the remainder, changing the mob clears the stores, the broken item carries them, and the unfed twin in the other dimension keeps its zeros.

The crafter and spawner ticks now act in the dimension the tick runs in rather than in whichever dimension happens to hold a matching block at those coordinates. With the same machine at the same position in two loaded dimensions the defect was sharper than a wrong choice: the spawner paid its energy and spawned nothing, because a level that is not in place refuses a spawn, so it silently died while the twin stood idle. Proven by placing a crafter and a spawner at identical coordinates in the End and the Overworld, feeding only the End pair, and reading both back through their own dimension: the End crafter crafts twelve planks for its three logs and the Overworld twin stays empty, the End spawner produces its zombie and spends its eight hundred while the twin stays at zero, and a selftest that expects zero there fails.

Slice 4, the spawner: a machine that sets a mob and spawns it on the neighbour its facing names, at the cost the mob's own recipe declares, with the mob chosen by a data recipe rather than a menu. The jar ships seventy such recipes, not the hundred our notes guessed, and all seventy travel byte for byte, because they carry the ingredient lists in a form this port deliberately never parses. Proven in game with the counterfactual on the same machine: with no energy it spawns nothing across sixty ticks and its counter stays at zero, and with the eight hundred its zombie recipe costs it spawns exactly one zombie within five blocks and leaves nothing in the buffer; a blaze costs a thousand and sets the second spawn's offsets. An absent mob is refused with the recipe count named, and an unknown id is refused before any energy is spent. That last point is a defect this port does not reproduce: upstream consumes the energy and clears the matter amounts before it checks whether the mob exists, so a recipe for an absent entity costs everything for a spawn that never happens. This port pays only once the spawn has answered.
First release

projects.name: Right-Click Crops
projects.summary: Right-click harvest for 16 plant families, with replanting and individual settings.
projects.description:
Harvest mature plants with a right-click, replant crops, and keep your garden growing.

### Features
- Supports 16 plant families.
- Replants crops using one planting item from the harvest, or from your inventory.
- Keeps the base of tall plants and the stems of pumpkins and melons.
- Lets you enable or disable each plant separately in **Options > Mods > Right-Click Crops > Config**.

### Supported plants
Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa, torchflower, pitcher crop, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp, twisting vines, weeping vines, pumpkin and melon.

### Good to know
- Harvesting works in survival, one targeted plant at a time.
- Without a suitable planting item, the crop is harvested but not replanted.
- Torchflower needs spare seeds; pitcher crop needs spare pitcher pods.
- Twisting and weeping vines can drop nothing when harvested by hand. Use shears for guaranteed drops.
- Bone meal, ordinary breaking and planting, sweet berries and glow berries keep their normal behaviour.

### Compatibility
For Minecraft 26.3. A WebAssembly mod: install it on the launcher's Mods page, with nothing to build. Install it on every player's game for LAN play. Settings from the old native versions do not carry over. Tested Horizon builds and results: [Validation](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops/blob/main/VALIDATION.md).


[Watch the demo](https://youtu.be/kll-qvj5s54) · [Harvesting guide](https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops/blob/main/docs/harvesting.md)

projects.description:
A port of [Roots Classic](https://github.com/Lothrazar/RootsClassic) by Elucent,
Lothrazar and Mrbysco for Horizon. This first slice is **the herbs and their
first uses** — the foraging loop and the food, not yet the rituals.

**Implemented so far**

  place on soil, refuse stone and drop themselves; sixteen carried ids in all.
- The jar's herb-forage table as a global loot modifier (API 75 `loot_drops`)
  at the jar's own configurable 1/N chances: broken short grass may add an old
  root, a last-age wheat/carrots/potatoes/beetroots a verdant sprig, ripe nether
  wart an infernal bulb, a chorus flower a dragon's eye, and leaves that dropped

  jar's nutrition, saturation and eaten effects: nightshade poisons, elderberry
  clears all effects, the dragon's eye teleports the eater, redcurrant heals 2
  and the healing poultice 5 (always edible).

  salad and healing poultice — with the `c:crops/wheat` tag they need, and a
  Roots Classic creative tab.

**Not yet ported**

  source in this slice (creative or `/give` only).
- The Bark Knife and the six barks; the Mortar, Pestle spell crafting and the

- The Altar and every ritual, the ten standing stones and their block entities,

  tools and the two armour sets; the Phantom Skeleton.

One file installs both halves: the `.hnmod` carries the content (blocks, items,

travel inside the distributed archive (`mixins/rootsclassic/LICENSE` and

versions.changelog: Slice 2, the powder chain: growth powder (dirt to grass, a young crop to growth) and mutating powder with its three mutations — flare orchid, midnight bloom and radiant daisy — their two recipes and four convention tags. That closes the note that the three herbs had no survival-obtainable source. One content trap was found and fixed: the growth powder first used the redstone template, which made it a block item that placed a wire; both powders are plain items now. One double-spend was found in game and fixed: answering `PASS` let the click be re-issued, so one click spent two powders; the powder now answers `SuccessServer` when it acts. Proven in game: both recipes craft with their ingredients consumed and their wrong-ingredient controls stay empty; dirt becomes grass for one powder while stone spends nothing; wheat goes from age 0 to 5 for one; each mutation sets its block, discards the ingredients, spends the powder and applies the jar's Fire and skip-tick data plus blindness, while a bystander item entity and a midnight-instead-of-noon run leave it alone.
First release: the three herbs, the herb-forage table, the food items with their eaten effects, and the five recipes

projects.name: RReturn
projects.summary: Rewinds the world and player state to the last checkpoint on death.
projects.description:
Rewinds the world and player state to the last checkpoint when the player dies. Blocks, containers, entities, weather, time, dimensions, and inventory are restored to their state at the checkpoint.

### How it works
- **Return by Death:** On fatal damage, the world rolls back to the last checkpoint instead of showing the death screen.
- **Checkpoints:** An initial checkpoint is created when entering a world. New checkpoints are saved automatically during safe periods, after combat, and after defeating a boss, or on a fixed timer.
- **Multiplayer modes:** On a LAN or server world, a key player's death rewinds the world for everyone on it. Supports single key player, multiple key players, all players, or rotating key player, with an optional rollback cooldown.
- **Manual control:** With cheats enabled, `F6` (`/rreturn set`) creates a checkpoint, `F7` (`/rreturn load`) rolls back, and `F8` switches the key player mode.
- **World data:** Checkpoints and logs are stored inside the world save folder (`rreturn/`) and mod settings are saved in the client configuration.

Settings and keybinds are in **Options > Mods**.

projects.summary: Keypads, reinforced doors and the rest of SecurityCraft's block protection, ported to Horizon.
projects.description:
A port of [SecurityCraft](https://github.com/Geforce132/SecurityCraft) (MIT, by Geforce132) for Horizon. This first slice brings the **keypad** and the **reinforced iron door**.

**Implemented so far**

- Place a keypad, open it and type a code on its on-screen keypad. The code is stored **salted and hashed**, never in plain text: the typed digits live in memory only while the screen is open, and the block entity's saved compound holds just the salt and the digest — closing the screen, submitting, or saving the world cannot write a passcode to disk.
- The keypad powers a redstone signal for 60 ticks when the right code is entered, which opens a reinforced iron door placed beside it.
- A wrong code leaves the door closed; a keypad with no door powers but opens nothing; an empty code stores nothing; a bare hand cannot open the reinforced door.
- `/securitycraft info|code` for testing and for setting a code without the screen, with the carried keypad and door blocks, models, textures, language and recipe inside the one `.hnmod`.

**Not yet ported**

- The owner and allowlist system (owner-only editing, allowlist modules, the `SECURITYCRAFT_OWNER` checks), and every other module.
- The reinforced block family beyond the iron door: reinforced stone, glass, stairs, slabs and the rest.
- The remaining machines (keycard reader, retina scanner, camera, alarm, laser block, inventory scanner, …) and their screens.
- The keypad's screen is drawn from shape primitives (panel, key grid, digits) rather than the jar's GUI atlas.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/securitycraft/LICENSE`.

The testing needed a harness-only command that puts a stranger's identity in front of the block, because a single-player run has only one player; that command is op-gated and exists only for the leg. projects.name: Server Flags
projects.summary: A flag beside each server in the Multiplayer list for the country it's hosted in
projects.description:
A small flag beside each server in your Multiplayer list for the country it's hosted in. Hover the flag for the country's name, and pick servers close to you for a better ping at a glance.

- **Pixel-art flags** after each server's name, or on its icon when the name is long.
- **67 drawn flags**, the countries servers are most often hosted in; any other country shows its two-letter code.
- **Country name on hover**, like "Germany (DE)".
- Servers on your own network are never looked up.
- A grey **?** marks a server whose location can't be shown; hover it for why (an ad blocker blocking the lookup, DDoS protection, or a wrong address).

Settings in Mods > Server Flags > Config: lookups on/off, flag position, hover tooltip, codes for countries without a flag.

**Privacy:** to know where a server is, the mod resolves its address and sends only that IP address to https://api.country.is (open source, no account or key), which answers with a country code. Once per server per game session, in the background, only while "Look up server locations" is on; a lookup that couldn't get through (an ad blocker, no connection) is tried again a minute later, three times at most, so the same IP can be sent up to three more times. Nothing about you, your account or your other servers is sent, and local-network addresses (also IPv4 written as IPv6) are never looked up. Switching the setting off stops new lookups; one already on its way may still finish. The request runs the system's curl with --disable, so the user's own curl config (.curlrc) is not used.

The request is made by the system's `curl` program (built into Windows 10 and 11, macOS and most Linux systems), run with only the service address and the server's IP. Rust's HTTPS libraries bring a second copy of a native library the game already has, which a mod may not link.

Horizon has no hook for the server list, so besides the mod API this mod patches one game function (draw_title_screen_with_post_hook) to draw the flags. It works on the Horizon build it is made for.

Source: https://github.com/selfmonoraque5/server-flags

Inspired by Server Country Flags by Khajiitos (https://modrinth.com/mod/server-country-flags). Written from scratch for Horizon: it contains none of its code or images (the flags are drawn in code) and is not made or endorsed by Khajiitos. Locations by country.is.

Built for Nightly 2026-11-21 8f83e5c: the game function it patches is unchanged from 5ef7734, so there are no code changes beyond 2.0.2's privacy fixes to the country lookup.

Rebuilt on Horizon's new mod API (the .hmod SDK) for Nightly 2026-11-19 5ef7734, with its game patches checked for that build. Settings now open from Mods > Server Flags > Config and start from the defaults once. The country lookup ignores the user's own curl config, never sends local-network addresses written as IPv6, and stops if lookups are switched off while it resolves.

projects.name: sfm
projects.summary: A Horizon port of sfm.
projects.description:
A port of [Super Factory Manager](https://github.com/TeamDman/SuperFactoryManager) (MPL-2.0, by TeamDman and the SFM contributors) for Horizon. This first slice is the **Factory Manager** and the plain inventory cable: the program text, the label table the upstream disk holds, a compiled subset of SFML, and the item movement one program tick makes over the cable network.

**Implemented so far**

- The Factory Manager and the plain inventory cable, with the carried models, textures and language entries, shipped inside the one `.hnmod`.
- A compiled SFML subset: `NAME "…"`, `EVERY <n> TICKS|SECONDS DO … END` (`SECONDS` is 20 ticks, offset 0, `LOCAL` alignment), `INPUT`/`OUTPUT` with an optional quantity, `EACH`, `RETAIN n [EACH]`, a resource list (`stone`, `minecraft:redstone`, `*ingot*`), `EXCEPT …`, a label list (bare or quoted), a `SIDE` list, and `FORGET`.
- Upstream's defaults: `INPUT` takes all and leaves none, `OUTPUT` accepts all it is offered.
- Item movement between the labelled inventories of one cable network, one program tick at a time, through the pin's hopper-rule helpers.

**Not yet ported**

- The rest of the language: `IF`/`THEN`/`ELSE`, `REDSTONE TRIGGER`, `EMPTY SLOTS IN`, slot ranges, `ROUND ROBIN`, per-block `EACH`, quoted regex patterns, `MAX`/`EACH` on retention per id combination, `WITH` clauses, fluid/energy/chemical/redstone resources, and the `SIDE` forms `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FRONT`/`BACK` (they parse and name no face here).
- The rest of the content: the disk, label gun, network tool, form and form base, printing press, buffers, water tank, XP goop and shard, the fancy/tough/tunnelled cables, every facade, their recipes, loot and advancements, `c:` tag compatibility, and the Manager's and printing press's GUIs and data recipes.

projects.name: Silent Gear
projects.summary: Assemble a pickaxe from a blueprint, head and rod; its stats fold the material properties.
projects.description:
A port of [Silent Gear](https://github.com/SilentChaos512/Silent-Gear) (MIT, by SilentChaos512) for Horizon. This first slice is gear assembly and the tool stat block, for **one tool**: the pickaxe.

**Implemented so far**

- `/silentgear assemble pickaxe <head> <rod>` assembles a pickaxe from a carried blueprint, head and rod; the three are taken from the inventory (then the off hand) and consumed.
- The pickaxe's stats are folded from each material's properties with Silent Gear's own maths — weighted average, max, multiply-base, multiply-total and add, clamped — and the result is written into the item's `silentgear:gear` component.
- The material table is the jar's own data for iron, wood, stone, diamond, gold, flint and the empty netherite entry.
- The two-part recipe chain is craftable: `silentgear:blueprint_paper` (4 paper + a blue dye, from the jar), the pickaxe blueprint from it, the heads and the rods.
- `/silentgear stats` prints the held gear's folded stats, tier and durability.

**Not yet ported, and one hard limitation**

- **The assembled pickaxe always behaves as a vanilla iron pickaxe.** The pin has no per-stack tool stats — a tool's speed, harvest tier and durability are read from the item, not from the stack's components (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §3) — so the folded numbers are a readout, not the mining behaviour. Assembly refuses a head/rod combination whose folded stats differ from the vanilla iron pickaxe rather than silently producing an item that would not honour them. This is the slice's biggest gap.
- The other tools and armour, traits, grading, salvage, compound parts and the custom recipe types, the blueprint book and the gear-slot system are later slices.

MIT; the original copyright and permission notices travel inside the archive at `mixins/silentgear/LICENSE`.

projects.name: Simple Backups
projects.summary: Scheduled, on-disk backups of the whole world, with retention. A backup saves the open world, then a worker thread walks the world folder into a…
projects.description:
A Horizon port of Simple Backups 1.21-4.0.30: scheduled, on-disk backups of the server's world, with retention. A backup saves the open world, a worker thread walks the world folder into a `.zip.part`, publishes it by renaming, and the oldest archives are pruned down to the configured count. Upstream: https://github.com/ChaoticTrials/SimpleBackups — licence **Apache-2.0**.

**Implemented so far**

- The schedule counts server ticks when `interval_ticks` is set and otherwise uses `interval_minutes` of wall clock, with 0 disabling it, and due checks run at the end of a running tick.
- A save is requested from the open levels before the copy, and the copy starts only when the save cycle reports back.
- A worker thread writes `<world>/backups/<world>_<UTC>.zip.part` and publishes it by renaming, skipping `session.lock`, `.part` and `.tmp` files, symlinks and the backups folder.
- Retention prunes only `<world>_*.zip` files, oldest first, until `keep` remain, and never touches foreign files or a partial archive.
- A copy that a save overlapped is thrown away and redone, up to two retries, instead of publishing a possibly half-replaced region file; with retries off it is published and `/simplebackups status` reports `stale=true`.
- `/simplebackups backup [quiet]`, `status` and `list` work at permission level 2, a manual backup ignores `enabled`, and `config/simplebackups.toml` carries the schedule, `keep`, `compression_level`, `save_before_backup`, `retry_on_save`, `broadcast`, `backups_dir` and the ignore lists.
- Paths are hardened: an absolute or parent-traversing `backups_dir` is refused, and a backups folder or staging file that resolves outside the world is never written through.
- The package was proven in game at 0.2.1 with a control run that fails without it.

**Not yet ported**

- The consistency window cannot be closed, because there is no save-off or autosave-veto API at this pin, so a copy can still overlap an autosave and read a region file mid-replacement, a race upstream has too.
- Compression is unavailable, because an SDK mod may not add a registry crate, so the archive is written with `std` alone and entries are stored rather than deflated, which means `compression_level` is parsed and reported but cannot shrink a backup.
- The schedule is not persisted across restarts and starts at world open.
- Pause and unpause, `latest.log` capture, a disk-size cap, the empty-server policy, incremental backups, chains and merging, Cherished Worlds and mc2discord compat, regex ignores, and a synchronous copy mode are all deferred.
- Retention prunes after a successful publish and counts only the mod's own archives, both deliberate safety changes from upstream's delete-before-create behaviour.
- Naming is UTC and backups live in `<world>/backups`, where upstream used local time and the working directory.

Ported from the upstream mod (Apache-2.0); `LICENSE-NOTICE.md` records the credit and `LICENSE` the licence text.

Pinned to Horizon 0b14f8a and horizon-mixins e59da90.

projects.name: SkinsRestorer
projects.summary: Players change their skin on a Horizon server; the signed textures property is replaced before login.
projects.description:
SkinsRestorer lets players on a Horizon server change their skin. A stored skin replaces the player's signed `textures` property at login, before the server sends the profile, so the player's own client and everyone in the player list see it.

- `/skin set <name>` resolves a Minecraft account through the game's own profile resolver and stores its signed skin.
- `/skin clear` restores the player's own skin; `/skin update` refreshes the stored name; `/skin` shows what is stored.
- Operators can set or clear another player's skin.

The lookup runs in the background on the server tick, so the server never waits on Mojang. Skins are stored in `config/skinsrestorer/skins.json`.

This is a server-side native mod for the Horizon mod API. It is made for Nightly `8f83e5c` (2026-11-21), the first signed build with the `player_login_profile` hook and the `profiles` service from horizon-rust/horizon#18587. It is based on SkinsRestorer and licensed under GPL-3.0.

projects.name: solcarrot
projects.summary: A Horizon port of solcarrot.
projects.description:
A port of [Spice of Life: Carrot Edition](https://github.com/Cazsius/Spice-of-Life-Carrot-Edition) (LGPL-2.1, by Cazsius, Talonos, juliand665 and Mrbysco) for Horizon. This first slice is the food history and the max-health milestones it earns.

**Implemented so far**

- A history per player: a set of food **item ids**. A food is recorded when it finishes being eaten, and re-eating it adds nothing. Filtered foods (below the nutrition floor, blacklisted, or outside a non-empty whitelist) are still remembered but do not count, exactly as upstream's `FoodList.addFood` does.
- Milestones: `milestones` (default `5,10,15,20,25`) count unique counted foods. Each reached milestone grants `2 * hearts_per_milestone` health points on top of vanilla's 20; a `base_hearts` other than 10 adds `2 * (base_hearts - 10)` to the same modifier, so at the defaults 25 foods give 10 extra hearts.
- The modifier is reapplied on join, respawn and dimension change, and cleared on death when `reset_on_death` is on.
- The history is saved per world in `<world>/solcarrot/foods.tsv` (one line per player and food), flushed after every new food and on world close, so `/foodlist size` works for an offline player too.
- A `config/solcarrot.conf` `key = value` file with the upstream keys and defaults (`base_hearts`, `hearts_per_milestone`, `milestones`, `minimum_food_value`, the `blacklist`/`whitelist`, `reset_on_death`, `limit_progression_to_survival`).
- `/foodlist size|sync|clear [target]`.

**Not yet ported**

- The **food book** item, its recipe and its screen: the whole client half, with its tooltips, progress list and the "next milestone" line.
- The client sync packet upstream sends when the history changes; the server keeps the authority and `/foodlist sync` refreshes the count.
- Sounds and particles on a milestone.
- Using a per-player attachment instead of the world text file (the pin's attachments are online-only, while the file keeps `/foodlist` working for offline players).

LGPL-2.1-only, like the original; the licence text and the original copyright notice travel inside the archive, and the complete corresponding source is in the port repository.
